According to Masonick, it is a vivid example of convergent evolution in which the same predatory menace repeatedly drove the moths to adapt similar behaviors through different anatomical routes.
paras.zh: 作者估计，在大约 500 万至 3000 万年前，生殖器产生的超声波独立进化了至少四次、最多七次。根据共济会的说法，这是趋同进化的一个生动例子，其中相同的掠食性威胁反复驱使飞蛾通过不同的解剖路线适应类似的行为。

paras.en: But the evolutionary arms race was not a one-way street, he points out. Several hawkmoth lineages that shifted toward twilight or daytime activity subsequently lost their specialized sound-producing machinery.
paras.zh: 但他指出，进化军备竞赛并不是一条单行道。一些转向黄昏或白天活动的天蛾谱系随后失去了专门的发声机制。

paras.en: “It goes to show how intense bat predation is on insects,” Masonick says. “It’s been a major driver of insect evolution.”
paras.zh: “这表明蝙蝠对昆虫的捕食有多强烈，”梅索尼克说。 “它是昆虫进化的主要驱动力。”

articles.title: How octopuses squeeze through tiny openings, step by step
articles.author: Nora Bradford

paras.en: Octopuses have made many a great escape. Remember Inky, who fled from New Zealand’s national aquarium?
paras.zh: 章鱼帮助许多人成功逃脱。还记得逃离新西兰国家水族馆的 Inky 吗？

paras.en: The cephalopods can Houdini their way out of tanks and off boats by squeezing through narrow slits and incredibly tiny holes. Now researchers know exactly how some octopuses pull it off. These masterful getaways involve a consistent, step-by-step game plan, researchers report November 5 in the Journal of Experimental Biology.
paras.zh: 头足类动物可以通过狭窄的缝隙和极其微小的孔洞从坦克和船上逃脱。现在研究人员确切地知道一些章鱼是如何做到这一点的。研究人员在 11 月 5 日的《实验生物学杂志》上报告说，这些巧妙的度假活动需要一个一致的、循序渐进的游戏计划。

paras.en: Octopuses are mostly squishy muscle, allowing them to shape-shift, though they do have some rigid body parts. Not many scientists have studied how these animals squirm through small openings, says Robyn Crook, an evolutionary biologist at San Francisco State University who was not involved in the research. “It’s one of the most characteristic behaviors of octopuses in popular awareness, but the strategies octopuses use have not really been examined systematically.”
paras.zh: 章鱼主要是柔软的肌肉，使它们能够变形，尽管它们确实有一些坚硬的身体部位。旧金山州立大学的进化生物学家罗宾·克鲁克（Robyn Crook）没有参与这项研究，他说，没有多少科学家研究过这些动物如何在小开口中蠕动。 “这是公众意识中章鱼最具特色的行为之一，但章鱼使用的策略尚未真正得到系统的研究。”

paras.en: Sneaking through small spaces isn’t just a party trick for octopuses, says Michael Kuba, a biologist at the University of Naples Federico II in Italy. The animals use that skill to find hidden food and to avoid becoming food themselves.
paras.zh: 意大利那不勒斯费德里克二世大学的生物学家迈克尔·库巴说，潜入狭小的空间不仅仅是章鱼的聚会把戏。动物利用这种技能来寻找隐藏的食物并避免自己成为食物。

paras.en: Kuba and his colleagues observed how three common octopuses (Octopus vulgaris) and four Mayan octopuses (Octopus maya) approached small holes. For each individual, the team measured the distance between the octopus’s eyes as an indicator of the size of their most rigid cartilage around their brain. Then the researchers designed acrylic boxes with holes that were slightly smaller or larger than that eye-to-eye measurement. They plopped the octopuses inside and watched what happened.
paras.zh: 库巴和他的同事观察了三只普通章鱼（Octopus vulgaris）和四只玛雅章鱼（Octopus maya）如何接近小洞。对于每个章鱼，研究小组测量了章鱼眼睛之间的距离，作为其大脑周围最坚硬的软骨大小的指标。然后，研究人员设计了带有孔的丙烯酸盒子，这些孔比眼睛对眼睛的测量稍小或稍大。他们把章鱼放进去，观察发生了什么。

paras.en: Octopuses have slightly different escape how-tos, depending on the size of the hole they are squeezing through. Here, a common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) wriggles through a space just a little bit bigger than their most rigid body parts. It takes just three steps for the octopus to free itself from the acrylic box.
paras.zh: 章鱼的逃生方法略有不同，具体取决于它们挤过的洞的大小。在这里，一只普通章鱼（Octopus vulgaris）在一个比其最坚硬的身体部位稍大一点的空间中蠕动。章鱼只需三步就可以从亚克力盒子中解脱出来。

paras.en: Common octopuses used one of two escape strategies depending on the hole’s size. When the hole was wider than the distance between their eyes, the octopuses pushed themselves through it in three steps. First, they snuck one or two arms through the hole and then threaded a couple more arms through. Finally, they used the arms that they had already snaked through the hole to push against the box and yank their head and the rest of their arms through in one fell swoop. The whole operation took a few seconds.
paras.zh: 普通章鱼根据洞的大小使用两种逃跑策略中的一种。当洞比它们的眼睛之间的距离还宽时，章鱼就分三步将自己推了进去。首先，他们将一两只手臂从洞里偷偷塞进去，然后再将几只手臂穿进去。最后，他们用已经从洞里钻出来的手臂推着箱子，把自己的头和剩下的手臂一下子拽了进去。整个操作持续了几秒钟。

paras.en: When the hole was narrower, common octopuses added a fourth step. They shoved all of their arms through the hole first and then squished their head and bulbous mantle through.
paras.zh: 当洞变窄时，普通章鱼会增加第四步。他们先把所有的手臂都塞进洞里，然后把头和球状的斗篷压进去。

paras.en: When a hole is smaller than their most rigid body parts, common octopuses add a fourth step to wrestle their bodies through an opening.
paras.zh: 当一个洞比它们最坚硬的身体部位还小时，普通章鱼会增加第四步，通过一个开口来扭动自己的身体。

paras.en: Mayan octopuses behaved more cautiously than the common octopuses. When confronted with the narrower hole, Mayan octopuses didn’t even attempt to fit inside of it. They usually ignored it. This difference between the species could stem from their biology or how they’ve adapted to their environments, Kuba says. Mayan octopuses live in sandy, rocky areas, so while they might disappear under rocks, they don’t often need to cram through holes, he says.
paras.zh: 玛雅章鱼的行为比普通章鱼更加谨慎。当面对较窄的洞时，玛雅章鱼甚至没有试图钻进去。他们通常会忽略它。库巴说，物种之间的这种差异可能源于它们的生物学特性或它们如何适应环境。他说，玛雅章鱼生活在沙地、岩石地区，因此虽然它们可能会消失在岩石下，但它们并不经常需要钻进洞里。

paras.en: The team hopes these escape artists will inspire new soft robots that can morph their shape to fit through tiny spaces, says Wenci Xin, a robotics researcher at the National University of Singapore. “This incredible capability could enable robots to overcome environmental limitations and enter spaces that are difficult to reach.”
paras.zh: 新加坡国立大学机器人研究员 Wenci Xin 表示，该团队希望这些逃脱艺术家能够激发新的软机器人的灵感，这些机器人可以改变自己的形状以适应狭小的空间。 “这种令人难以置信的能力可以使机器人克服环境限制并进入难以到达的空间。”

paras.en: Studying how octopuses navigate different types of holes may provide additional clues for robots, Crook says. For instance, the cephalopods may take a different tack for openings that are more like slits or tubes than holes.
paras.zh: 克鲁克说，研究章鱼如何穿过不同类型的洞可能为机器人提供更多线索。例如，头足类动物可能会采用不同的方法来处理更像狭缝或管子而不是孔的开口。

paras.en: Currently, robots built to fit through tiny holes tend to be snake-shaped, but further research on these eight-armed contortionists could unlock other configurations.
paras.zh: 目前，用于穿过小孔的机器人往往是蛇形的，但对这些八臂柔术演员的进一步研究可以解锁其他配置。

articles.title: World First: Underwater Volcano Off US Coast Generates Net-Positive Electricity
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: An engineering team lowered a generator to the ocean floor and ran it using heat from an underwater volcano. They wanted to find out whether it could produce more electricity than it needed to operate.
paras.zh: 一个工程团队将一台发电机放入海底，并利用水下火山的热量来运行它。他们想知道它是否能产生比运行所需更多的电力。

paras.en: For 8.7 seconds, the system did just that.
paras.zh: 在 8.7 秒的时间里，系统就这么做了。

paras.en: Seattle-based Endurance Energy announced the results of its Adélie experiment on October 19 in a company press release.
paras.zh: 总部位于西雅图的 Endurance Energy 于 10 月 19 日在公司新闻稿中公布了阿德利实验的结果。

paras.en: The test took place at Axial Seamount, an underwater volcano about 480 kilometers (300 miles) off Oregon. Here, hot springs emerge from the seabed roughly 1,500 meters (5,000 feet) below the ocean's surface.
paras.zh: 此次测试在轴向海山进行，这是一座距离俄勒冈州约 480 公里（300 英里）的水下火山。这里的温泉从海面以下约 1,500 米（5,000 英尺）的海底涌出。

paras.en: The water gets its heat from molten rock beneath the volcano. Seawater seeps into cracks in the seabed, heats up underground, and flows back into the ocean through openings called hydrothermal vents.
paras.zh: 水从火山下方的熔岩中获取热量。海水渗入海底裂缝，在地下升温，然后通过称为热液喷口的开口流回海洋。

paras.en: Endurance's engineers set out to capture some of that heat. On land, geothermal power plants already use hot water or steam from underground to generate electricity. Heat drives a spinning machine called a turbine, which turns a generator. This energy source doesn't depend on sunshine or wind.
paras.zh: Endurance 的工程师着手捕获部分热量。在陆地上，地热发电厂已经使用地下的热水或蒸汽来发电。热量驱动称为涡轮机的纺纱机，涡轮机带动发电机。这种能源不依赖于阳光或风。

paras.en: To make it work on the seabed, the team first needed enough hot water flowing through its equipment. Engineers drilled a well extending 16 meters (52 feet) beneath the ocean floor, installed a pipe inside it, and cemented it in place.
paras.zh: 为了使其在海底工作，该团队首先需要有足够的热水流过其设备。工程师们在海底钻了一口深达 16 米（52 英尺）的井，在井内安装了一根管道，并将其固定到位。

paras.en: Water emerged at about 260 °C (500 °F), but its flow was too restricted to run the generator.
paras.zh: 水的温度约为 260 °C (500 °F)，但其流量太有限，无法运行发电机。

paras.en: The engineers connected Adélie to a nearby natural vent. Heat for the successful test therefore came from water already flowing out of the seabed.
paras.zh: 工程师将阿德利连接到附近的自然通风口。因此，成功测试的热量来自已经从海底流出的水。

paras.en: During the September 27 experiment, that water was approximately 281 °C (538 °F). High pressure at this depth allows water to remain liquid well above its surface boiling temperature of 100 °C (212 °F).
paras.zh: 在 9 月 27 日的实验中，水温约为 281 °C (538 °F)。该深度的高压使水在远高于其表面沸腾温度 100 °C (212 °F) 时仍能保持液态。

paras.en: As the system ran, its turbine reached approximately 26,000 revolutions per minute.
paras.zh: 当系统运行时，其涡轮机达到每分钟约 26,000 转。

paras.en: The team controlled the equipment from Seattle. Scientists already monitor the active underwater volcano using instruments connected to shore.
paras.zh: 该团队从西雅图控制设备。科学家们已经使用连接到海岸的仪器监测这座活水下火山。

paras.en: An existing undersea cable network called the Regional Cabled Array, operated by the University of Washington, provided the connection for Endurance's experiment.
paras.zh: 由华盛顿大学运营的一个名为“区域电缆阵列”的现有海底电缆网络为“耐力”号的实验提供了连接。

paras.en: The pumps and other components also consumed electricity. After subtracting that demand, the company's press release reported a median surplus of about 2 kilowatts during the 8.7-second interval, with a peak of 16.5 kilowatts.
paras.zh: 泵和其他部件也消耗电力。扣除该需求后，该公司的新闻稿称，在 8.7 秒的时间间隔内，中位剩余电量约为 2 千瓦，峰值为 16.5 千瓦。

paras.en: Researchers have generated electricity from seafloor vents before. In a study published in Applied Energy in 2016, a Chinese team described a device that converted the temperature difference between hot vent water and cold seawater into electricity.
paras.zh: 研究人员此前曾利用海底喷口发电。在2016年《应用能源》杂志上发表的一项研究中，一个中国团队描述了一种将热喷口水和冷海水之间的温差转化为电能的装置。

paras.en: The device continuously produced 2.6–3.9 watts during its field test and powered a data logger and an LED lamp.
paras.zh: 该设备在现场测试期间持续产生 2.6-3.9 瓦的功率，并为数据记录器和 LED 灯供电。

paras.en: Endurance's longer-term goal is to supply customers on land.
paras.zh: Endurance 的长期目标是为陆地客户提供服务。

paras.en: The company says its first commercial project is being developed in Tonga, a Pacific island nation whose electricity grid relies largely on imported diesel. It is targeting first power in 2027.
paras.zh: 该公司表示，其第一个商业项目正在汤加开发，汤加是一个太平洋岛国，其电网主要依赖进口柴油。它的目标是在 2027 年首次发电。

paras.en: Reaching that goal will require much longer operation. Adélie's run stopped when a safety system protecting its battery from excessive current activated. About 10 minutes later, a pump power cable failed during a restart attempt.
paras.zh: 实现这一目标将需要更长的时间。当保护电池免受过大电流影响的安全系统启动时，阿德利的运行停止了。大约 10 分钟后，泵电源线在尝试重新启动时出现故障。

paras.en: "Gentoo, Endurance's next 100kW test generator, is an upgraded Adélie. It deploys this winter and targets higher power and longer runs," Endurance founder and CEO Andrew Redd told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: Endurance 创始人兼首席执行官安德鲁·雷德 (Andrew Redd) 告诉 ScienceAlert：“Endurance 的下一款 100kW 测试发电机 Gentoo 是 Adélie 的升级版。它于今年冬天部署，目标是更高功率和更长时间的运行。”

paras.en: Redd said the updated equipment will address the battery protection and pump cable problems encountered during the test.
paras.zh: 雷德表示，更新后的设备将解决测试过程中遇到的电池保护和泵电缆问题。

paras.en: "Endurance has a new drill coming online next year which will reach 500m depth at maximum," Redd said.
paras.zh: “Endurance 明年将推出一款新钻机，最大深度将达到 500m，”Redd 说道。

paras.en: That's about 1,640 feet, compared with the current drill's 80-meter (260-foot) maximum. The company expects deeper wells to provide greater water flow.
paras.zh: 这大约是 1,640 英尺，而当前钻机的最大深度为 80 米（260 英尺）。该公司预计更深的井将提供更大的水流量。

paras.en: Redd said the team still needs to achieve sustained generation from a drilled well and develop equipment that operates reliably for months or years.
paras.zh: 雷德表示，该团队仍然需要实现钻井的持续发电，并开发能够可靠运行数月或数年的设备。

paras.en: These figures describe electricity production during operation. They don't account for the energy spent on shipping, drilling, and installation. The measurements come from Endurance, and its announcement includes no peer-reviewed paper reporting the results.
paras.zh: 这些数字描述了运行期间的发电量。它们没有考虑运输、钻孔和安装所消耗的能源。这些测量结果来自 Endurance，其公告中没有报告结果的同行评审论文。

paras.en: Environmental questions also remain. Microbes around vents use chemicals for energy, and tubeworms and other animals depend on those microbes.
paras.zh: 环境问题也依然存在。喷口周围的微生物利用化学物质获取能量，而管虫和其他动物则依赖这些微生物。

paras.en: Endurance says it chose a drilling location away from the vent chimneys and nearby animals. Its monitoring found no notable change in the life around the site, the company reported.
paras.zh: 耐力公司表示，它选择的钻探地点远离通风烟囱和附近的动物。该公司报告称，监测发现该地点周围的生活没有明显变化。

paras.en: According to the announcement, more than 40 water, rock, and mineral samples were sent to independent laboratories for analysis. Longer-term effects remain to be established.
paras.zh: 公告称，40多个水、岩石和矿物样本被送往独立实验室进行分析。长期影响仍有待确定。

paras.en: "We recognize that larger systems running continuously over years could affect the surrounding water column, biological communities and seafloor habitat," Redd said.
paras.zh: 雷德说：“我们认识到，持续运行多年的大型系统可能会影响周围的水体、生物群落和海底栖息地。”

paras.en: The company is working with independent researchers on further analysis and studies, Redd added.
paras.zh: 雷德补充说，该公司正在与独立研究人员合作进行进一步的分析和研究。

paras.en: The experiment showed that the generator could briefly produce more electricity than it consumed. The next test is whether it can keep running. Longer deployments will also help establish how it affects the surrounding ocean.
paras.zh: 实验表明，发电机可以短暂地产生比消耗的更多的电力。接下来的测试是能否继续运行。更长的部署也将有助于确定它如何影响周围的海洋。

articles.title: At 91, Julie Andrews Swears by One Habit Linked to 18% Lower Dementia Risk
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Julie Andrews is one of the most famous actresses in the world, and at age 91, she is still working creatively.
paras.zh: 朱莉·安德鲁斯 (Julie Andrews) 是世界上最著名的女演员之一，91 岁高龄的她仍在创作中。

paras.en: The long-celebrated star of Mary Poppins and The Sound of Music may no longer be in front of the screen, but she continues voice acting for Bridgerton, and she just published a new children's book with her daughter.
paras.zh: 这位《欢乐满人间》和《音乐之声》中久负盛名的明星可能不再出现在银幕前，但她继续为布里奇顿配音，并且刚刚与女儿出版了一本新的儿童读物。

paras.en: In a recent interview with InStyle, Andrews said she mostly keeps working and creating to keep her brain alive.
paras.zh: 在最近接受 InStyle 采访时，安德鲁斯表示，她主要通过工作和创作来保持大脑活力。

paras.en: Emerging evidence suggests she's on to something.
paras.zh: 新出现的证据表明她正在做某件事。

paras.en: In 2021, an international team of researchers examined the association between cognitively stimulating work and the subsequent risk of dementia.
paras.zh: 2021 年，一个国际研究小组研究了认知刺激工作与随后患痴呆症风险之间的关联。

paras.en: They brought together data from more than 100,000 people in the United Kingdom, Europe, and the United States.
paras.zh: 他们汇集了英国、欧洲和美国超过 100,000 人的数据。

paras.en: After adjusting for other risk factors, they found that those participants with cognitively stimulating jobs had an 18 percent lower risk of dementia.
paras.zh: 在调整其他风险因素后，他们发现那些从事认知刺激工作的参与者患痴呆症的风险降低了 18%。

paras.en: The findings are supported by a string of other studies, which suggest that staying cognitively stimulated in later life may be important for the aging brain.
paras.zh: 这些发现得到了一系列其他研究的支持，这些研究表明，在晚年保持认知刺激可能对衰老的大脑很重要。

paras.en: In 2023, for instance, scientists found that immediately after retirement, cognitive function declines at an accelerated rate.
paras.zh: 例如，到 2023 年，科学家发现，退休后，认知功能会加速下降。

paras.en: That isn't to say that the decline is due to retirement; it's just an association. But the timing is suspicious.
paras.zh: 这并不是说下降是由于退休所致；而是说，下降是由于退休造成的。这只是一个协会。但时机很可疑。

paras.en: It could be that people more cognitively capable are working into later age, or it may be that mentally stimulating work can help keep the brain fit and healthy.
paras.zh: 这可能是因为认知能力更强的人正在工作到更晚的年龄，或者可能是脑力刺激的工作有助于保持大脑的健康。

paras.en: Learning is, after all, known to support brain function in our younger years. Why not in our later years as well?
paras.zh: 毕竟，众所周知，学习可以支持我们年轻时的大脑功能。为什么不在我们晚年呢？

paras.en: Rachel Wu is a psychologist at the University of California, Riverside, who is researching how learning can boost cognition even in older age.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·吴（Rachel Wu）是加州大学河滨分校的心理学家，她正在研究学习如何提高老年人的认知能力。

paras.en: In an interview with the American Psychological Association earlier this year, she said that "there seems to be a societal expectation that adults are not supposed to be learning as much as children are."
paras.zh: 在今年早些时候接受美国心理学会采访时，她表示“社会似乎期望成年人不应该像孩子那样学习那么多。”

paras.en: She wondered: "What if adulthood is one very long summer slide, similar to what students experience during summer break?"
paras.zh: 她想知道：“如果成年期是一张很长的暑假幻灯片，就像学生在暑假期间经历的那样呢？”

paras.en: She and her colleagues published a study in 2023 that had older adults learn at least three new skills, such as Spanish, drawing, or music composition, over the course of three months.
paras.zh: 她和她的同事在 2023 年发表了一项研究，要求老年人在三个月的时间内学习至少三项新技能，例如西班牙语、绘画或音乐创作。

paras.en: At the end of the trial, participants showed improved cognitive performance. In fact, their scores were on par with a separate cohort of much younger adults.
paras.zh: 试验结束时，参与者的认知能力有所提高。事实上，他们的分数与另一组年轻得多的成年人的分数相当。

paras.en: "Our multiskill intervention may provide broad cognitive gains, akin to the benefits experienced earlier in the life span," the study authors concluded.
paras.zh: 研究作者总结道：“我们的多技能干预可能会带来广泛的认知收益，类似于生命早期经历的好处。”

paras.en: The findings suggest that challenging yourself cognitively in older age, as Julie Andrews does, could help keep the brain young.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，像朱莉·安德鲁斯那样，在老年时挑战自己的认知能力可以帮助保持大脑年轻。

paras.en: "I probably feel like in my 50s, honest to God," Andrews told Julia Louis-Dreyfus on her podcast Wiser Than Me at age 88.
paras.zh: “对上帝说实话，我可能感觉自己已经 50 多岁了，”88 岁的安德鲁斯在她的播客 Wiser Than Me 中告诉朱莉娅·路易斯-德雷福斯。

paras.en: "As long as the brain holds out, I'm doing okay."
paras.zh: “只要我的大脑还能坚持下去，我就一切都好。”

paras.en: During the podcast, Andrews explained that her father also was a lifelong learner. She got her love of books and writing from him.
paras.zh: 在播客中，安德鲁斯解释说，她的父亲也是一位终身学习者。她对书籍和写作的热爱是从他那里得到的。

paras.en: He studied a whole new language at age 76.
paras.zh: 76 岁时，他学习了一门全新的语言。

paras.en: Alexandra Touroutoglou is a neurologist at Harvard University who studies super-agers, or those who remain cognitively sprightly even into very old age.
paras.zh: 亚历山德拉·图鲁特格鲁 (Alexandra Touroutoglou) 是哈佛大学的神经学家，研究对象是超级老人，即那些即使到了高龄仍保持认知能力的人。

paras.en: "Anecdotally, talking with our participants, the super-agers say they really enjoy challenging themselves," she said in an interview with the Harvard Gazette earlier this year.
paras.zh: “有趣的是，在与我们的参与者交谈时，超级老人说他们真的很喜欢挑战自己，”她在今年早些时候接受《哈佛公报》采访时说道。

paras.en: "They don't want to sit in the background; they want to learn new things."
paras.zh: “他们不想坐在幕后；他们想学习新事物。”

paras.en: Growing older is inevitable, but that isn't to say a person has no control.
paras.zh: 变老是不可避免的，但这并不是说一个人无法控制。

paras.en: The 2024 Lancet Commission estimates that around 45 percent of dementia cases worldwide can be prevented or delayed with changes to certain lifestyle habits, medical conditions, or environmental factors.
paras.zh: 2024 年《柳叶刀》委员会估计，全球约 45% 的痴呆症病例可以通过改变某些生活习惯、医疗条件或环境因素来预防或延迟。

paras.en: Working with language, like reading or writing books, seems to be particularly worthwhile for the aging brain.
paras.zh: 与语言相关的工作，比如读书或写书，对于衰老的大脑来说似乎特别有价值。

paras.en: A recent study, published in Neurology earlier this year, followed nearly 2,000 older individuals from Illinois in the United States who did not have dementia at baseline.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候发表在《Neurology》上的一项最新研究对美国伊利诺伊州近 2000 名基线时未患有痴呆症的老年人进行了跟踪调查。

paras.en: After nearly eight years, 551 had developed Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 近八年后，551 人患上了阿尔茨海默病。

paras.en: Those who reported more frequent engagement in cognitive activities throughout their lifespan, like reading books, visiting libraries and museums, learning foreign languages, or using dictionaries, showed better cognitive outcomes in later life.
paras.zh: 那些在一生中更频繁地参与认知活动（例如读书、参观图书馆和博物馆、学习外语或使用词典）的人在以后的生活中表现出更好的认知结果。

paras.en: In fact, a higher lifetime score for cognitive enrichment was associated with a 38 percent lower risk of Alzheimer's, a 36 percent lower risk of mild cognitive impairment, and a delayed onset of cognitive decline by up to 7 years.
paras.zh: 事实上，认知丰富的终生得分越高，患阿尔茨海默病的风险就会降低 38%，轻度认知障碍的风险就会降低 36%，认知能力下降的发生时间会延迟长达 7 年。

paras.en: It also led to greater cognitive function later in life.
paras.zh: 它还导致了以后生活中更强大的认知功能。

paras.en: "Our findings are encouraging, suggesting that consistently engaging in a variety of mentally stimulating activities throughout life may make a difference in cognition," said co-author and neuropsychologist Andrea Zammit in February.
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果令人鼓舞，表明一生中持续参与各种精神刺激活动可能会对认知产生影响，”共同作者、神经心理学家安德里亚·扎米特 (Andrea Zammit) 在二月份说道。

paras.en: These findings support the idea of a 'cognitive reserve', which is sort of like a muscle reserve.
paras.zh: 这些发现支持“认知储备”的想法，这有点像肌肉储备。

paras.en: According to this concept, as a person ages, the more they have exercised their brain in the decades before, the more protected it is from decline.
paras.zh: 根据这个概念，随着一个人年龄的增长，他们在过去几十年里锻炼大脑的次数越多，大脑就越能免受衰退的影响。

paras.en: Related: The Links Between Napping And Dementia May Go Further Than We Realized
paras.zh: 相关：午睡和痴呆症之间的联系可能比我们意识到的更进一步

paras.en: In 2024, for instance, a study from Norway found that those with a history of cognitively stimulating occupations in their 30s, 40s, 50s, and 60s had a lower risk of mild cognitive impairment and dementia when they reached their 70s.
paras.zh: 例如，2024 年挪威的一项研究发现，那些在 30 多岁、40 多岁、50 多岁和 60 多岁从事过认知刺激职业的人在 70 多岁时患轻度认知障碍和痴呆的风险较低。

paras.en: Julie Andrews has spent her whole life stimulating her brain and pushing herself creatively.
paras.zh: 朱莉·安德鲁斯一生都在刺激她的大脑并推动自己发挥创造力。

paras.en: Even in her 90s, she chooses to keep learning to keep her brain fit and healthy.
paras.zh: 即使已经90多岁了，她仍然选择继续学习，以保持大脑健康。

paras.en: In exploring her passion for writing, Julie Andrews swallows her medicine with a spoonful of sugar.
paras.zh: 在探索她对写作的热情时，朱莉·安德鲁斯用一勺糖吞下了她的药。

articles.title: After 42 Years of Searching, Physicists Find Evidence of a One-in-10-Billion Particle Decay
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: We may be one gigantically small step closer to solving the most essential Universal questions, including what happened immediately after the Big Bang, where is dark matter hiding, and why does normal matter even exist?
paras.zh: 我们可能距离解决最基本的普遍问题又迈出了一大步，包括大爆炸后立即发生的事情，暗物质隐藏在哪里，以及为什么正常物质甚至存在？

paras.en: The increasing sensitivity of particle colliders like CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is allowing researchers to probe unprecedentedly deeper into the very structure of our reality.
paras.zh: 欧洲核子研究组织的大型强子对撞机 (LHC) 等粒子对撞机的灵敏度不断提高，使研究人员能够前所未有地更深入地探索我们现实的结构。

paras.en: Called the "zeptoverse," it may harbor undiscovered particles or forces existing at zeptometer scales, thousands of trillions of times thinner than a human hair, and cosmos-shaping quantum actions across time spans that are unimaginably small.
paras.zh: 它被称为“zeptoverse”，它可能蕴藏着未发现的粒子或力，存在于 zeptometer 尺度，比人类头发丝细数千万亿倍，并且在难以想象的小时间跨度上塑造宇宙的量子作用。

paras.en: After more than 40 years of effort, scientists have effectively fastened a knocker on the door of the zeptoverse, offering experimental evidence of an exceedingly elusive, unstable type of particle decay.
paras.zh: 经过 40 多年的努力，科学家们有效地在 zeptoverse 的大门上敲响了门环，为一种极其难以捉摸、不稳定的粒子衰变类型提供了实验证据。

paras.en: In a seminar held on November 3rd, and in a preprint paper on arXiv that has not yet been peer-reviewed, the LHCb Collaboration announced evidence of this phenomenon.
paras.zh: 在 11 月 3 日举行的研讨会上，以及在 arXiv 上尚未经过同行评审的预印本论文中，LHCb 合作组织公布了这一现象的证据。

paras.en: It's thought to occur only once in ten billion events involving the death of a certain "beauty" particle – odds substantially less likely than winning the lottery.
paras.zh: 据认为，在涉及某种“美丽”粒子死亡的百亿次事件中，这种情况只发生一次——几率比中彩票的可能性要小得多。

paras.en: This potential discovery, and a much more precise measurement of a previously observed sibling decay, provide "a powerful new test of the Standard Model and a window into potential new physics," explains Niladri Sahoo, particle physicist at the University of Birmingham and convener of the LHCb Very Rare Decays working group.
paras.zh: 伯明翰大学粒子物理学家、LHCb 极稀有衰变工作组召集人 Niladri Sahoo 解释说，这一潜在发现以及对先前观察到的同级衰变的更精确测量，为“标准模型提供了一次强大的新测试，并为了解潜在新物理学提供了一个窗口”。

paras.en: The experiment was conducted at the Large Hadron Collider Beauty (LHCb), a particle-hunting project situated along the sprawling subterranean LHC.
paras.zh: 该实验是在大型强子对撞机美景 (LHCb) 中进行的，这是一个位于庞大的地下大型强子对撞机沿线的粒子搜寻项目。

paras.en: It's now able to home in on such rare particle physics – sought since the 1980s – thanks to a recent update that significantly boosted its particle collision detection rate, as well as leveraging machine learning techniques to increase the signal-to-noise ratio that has drowned such attempted observations.
paras.zh: 它现在能够专注于这种自 20 世纪 80 年代以来一直在寻求的罕见粒子物理学，这要归功于最近的更新，显着提高了其粒子碰撞检测率，并利用机器学习技术来提高信噪比，从而淹没了此类观测尝试。

paras.en: The LHCb experiment detects decays using instruments like its eagle-eye VELO sub-detector, which is snugly situated less than a finger's width from the particle beam to better observe the zoo of exotic particles produced by near-light-speed collisions.
paras.zh: LHCb 实验使用鹰眼 VELO 子探测器等仪器来检测衰变，该子探测器与粒子束的距离小于手指宽度，以便更好地观察近光速碰撞产生的奇异粒子。

paras.en: So the scientists' big breakthrough is the potential detection of the decay of a particle known as a Bd meson into a muon and an anti-muon.
paras.zh: 因此，科学家们的重大突破是潜在地检测到一种称为 Bd 介子的粒子衰变为 μ 子和反 μ 子。

paras.en: The meson in question is composed of two weird particles, called a beauty quark and a down antiquark.
paras.zh: 所讨论的介子由两种奇怪的粒子组成，称为美夸克和下反夸克。

paras.en: Quarks come in six flavors, and two of them, called up and down quarks, combine in triads to form neutrons and protons.
paras.zh: 夸克有六种类型，其中两种称为上夸克和下夸克，以三合体形式结合形成中子和质子。

paras.en: The other quarks are more esoteric but essential for exploring the greatest Universal mysteries.
paras.zh: 其他夸克更加深奥，但对于探索最伟大的宇宙奥秘至关重要。

paras.en: Accordingly, "beauty quarks" were common in the soupy aftermath of the Big Bang, perhaps when the cosmos was just a hundredth of a billionth of a second old, but are naturally absent today.
paras.zh: 因此，“美夸克”在大爆炸后的混乱中很常见，也许当时宇宙只有十亿分之一秒的历史，但今天自然不存在了。

paras.en: So then where did the researchers get their hands on a beauty quark to make the meson and start the whole shebang?
paras.zh: 那么研究人员从哪里获得美夸克来制造介子并开始整个谢邦呢？

paras.en: First, they collided protons at near-light speed, producing an ephemeral spray of particles including many beauty quarks and down antiquarks, which don't like being alone, so they combine almost instantaneously via the strong nuclear force, which also binds quarks inside protons and neutrons.
paras.zh: 首先，它们以接近光速的速度碰撞质子，产生短暂的粒子喷雾，其中包括许多美夸克和下反夸克，它们不喜欢单独存在，因此它们几乎瞬间通过强核力结合在一起，强核力也将夸克束缚在质子和中子内部。

paras.en: These mesons are incredibly fleeting, decaying in one and a half trillionths of a second. But only one in every ten billion of these 'beauty-ful' decays yields the desired result: a muon and an anti-muon pop out of the energy of the quantum realm to conserve the energy-mass law.
paras.zh: 这些介子极其短暂，在万亿分之一秒内衰变。但这些“美丽”衰变中只有百亿分之一会产生预期的结果：一个μ子和一个反μ子从量子领域的能量中弹出，以遵守能量质量定律。

paras.en: These muons themselves only 'live' for around two millionths of a second before decaying into particles like electrons and positrons.
paras.zh: 这些μ子本身仅“存活”约百万分之二秒，然后衰变成电子和正电子等粒子。

paras.en: Claiming evidence for a phenomenon like this requires a significance level of three standard deviations, or "3 sigma," corresponding to a 0.3 percent chance that the result is a fluke.
paras.zh: 声称此类现象的证据需要三个标准差或“3 西格玛”的显着性水平，对应于结果是侥幸的可能性为 0.3%。

paras.en: This newest evidence, courtesy of the LHCb experiment from 2024 and 2025, combined with previous data gathered between 2011 and 2018, yields a comfortable significance level of 3.2 sigma.
paras.zh: 这一最新证据由 2024 年和 2025 年的 LHCb 实验提供，结合之前在 2011 年至 2018 年期间收集的数据，得出了 3.2 西格玛的显着性水平。

paras.en: Attaining the 'gold standard' 5-sigma significance value will require further research to confirm this decay. Future upgrades in the 2030s will boost the number of LHC collisions and again increase the data collection rate, by an order of magnitude.
paras.zh: 要达到“黄金标准”5-sigma 显着性值，需要进一步研究来证实这种衰减。 2030 年代的未来升级将增加大型强子对撞机碰撞的次数，并再次将数据收集率提高一个数量级。

paras.en: As the researchers summarize: "All results are consistent with [Standard Model] expectations and constrain new physics contributions at energy scales beyond those accessible through direct production at the LHC."
paras.zh: 正如研究人员总结的那样：“所有结果都与[标准模型]预期一致，并且限制了在大型强子对撞机直接生产之外的能量尺度上的新物理贡献。”

paras.en: This highlights that the results of this work align with the Standard Model, which explains much of our Universe but doesn't illuminate dark matter, or the slight asymmetry in normal matter and antimatter that prevented the entire cosmos from annihilating itself in a puff of energy after the Big Bang.
paras.zh: 这凸显了这项工作的结果与标准模型一致，该模型解释了我们宇宙的大部分，但没有阐明暗物质，或者正常物质和反物质中的轻微不对称性，这些不对称性阻止了整个宇宙在大爆炸后的一股能量中自我毁灭。

paras.en: It also tantalizes us with the suggestion that discovering novel physics may not rely on the LHC directly cranking out a new particle, but on indirect evidence, perhaps seen in other decay rates.
paras.zh: 它还向我们提出这样的建议：发现新的物理学可能并不依赖于大型强子对撞机直接产生新粒子，而是依赖于间接证据，也许可以在其他衰变率中看到。

paras.en: This has been the case in the past discoveries of the charm quark and the top quark, the latter of which is the heaviest of the quarks, about as massive as an entire gold atom.
paras.zh: 过去发现的粲夸克和顶夸克就是这种情况，后者是最重的夸克，大约有整个金原子的质量。

paras.en: "Seeing clear evidence for this rarest decay for the first time was thrilling," concludes Harry Cliff, a particle physicist at the University of Cambridge and leader of the analysis team.
paras.zh: “第一次看到这种最罕见的衰变的明确证据令人兴奋，”剑桥大学粒子物理学家、分析团队负责人哈利·克里夫总结道。

paras.en: "We're knocking on the door of the zeptoverse now. I can't wait to see what we find as we explore deeper."
paras.zh: “我们现在正在敲响 zeptoverse 的大门。我迫不及待地想看看我们在深入探索时会发现什么。”

paras.en: A preprint of the research paper is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究论文的预印本可在 arXiv 上找到。

articles.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation

paras.en: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
paras.zh: 科学家解开 30 年来的谜团，发现隐藏的炎症防御机制

paras.en: - Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
paras.zh: - 纪念斯隆凯特琳癌症中心

paras.en: - Scientists have solved a decades-old mystery and uncovered a hidden immune system defense that protects healthy cells from the very inflammation meant to fight infections. The surprising discovery could lead to new approaches for treating cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, and other conditions involving excessive inflammation.
paras.zh: - 科学家们解开了一个数十年之久的谜团，并发现了一种隐藏的免疫系统防御机制，可以保护健康细胞免受旨在对抗感染的炎症的侵害。这一令人惊讶的发现可能会带来治疗癌症、炎症性肠病和其他涉及过度炎症的疾病的新方法。

paras.en: Scientists have solved a biological mystery that remained unanswered for more than three decades, uncovering an unexpected way the immune system protects the body from its own inflammatory response. The breakthrough reveals that a chemical signal responsible for attracting immune cells to fight infections also helps prevent those same defenses from damaging healthy tissue.
paras.zh: 科学家们解开了三十多年来悬而未决的生物学谜团，揭示了免疫系统保护身体免受自身炎症反应影响的一种意想不到的方式。这一突破表明，负责吸引免疫细胞抵抗感染的化学信号也有助于防止这些防御损害健康组织。

paras.en: The discovery came from researchers at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK), who took an unusual approach to studying inflammation. Rather than relying on mice, a standard choice for biomedical research, they turned to zebrafish. That decision helped them identify a long-mysterious enzyme and uncover a protective mechanism that had previously escaped scientists.
paras.zh: 这一发现来自纪念斯隆凯特琳癌症中心 (MSK) 的研究人员，他们采用了一种不同寻常的方法来研究炎症。他们没有依赖小鼠（生物医学研究的标准选择），而是转向斑马鱼。这一决定帮助他们识别了一种长期神秘的酶，并揭示了一种此前科学家未能发现的保护机制。

paras.en: The findings, published October 7 in Nature, could advance research into cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, and asthma. They also raise the possibility of developing treatments that strengthen the body's natural defenses against inflammatory damage.
paras.zh: 该研究结果于 10 月 7 日发表在《自然》杂志上，可能会推进癌症、炎症性肠病和哮喘的研究。他们还提出了开发增强人体对炎症损伤的自然防御能力的治疗方法的可能性。

paras.en: A Scientific Mystery Dating Back to 1992
paras.zh: 一个可以追溯到 1992 年的科学谜团

paras.en: The mystery began in 1992, when researchers at McGill University investigated a molecule that helps direct immune cells toward sites of infection. Known as 5-oxoETE, or 5-oxo-6,8,11,14-eicosatetraenoic acid, this fatty signaling molecule acts as a chemical alert when the body needs to respond to a threat.
paras.zh: 这个谜团始于 1992 年，当时麦吉尔大学的研究人员研究了一种有助于引导免疫细胞前往感染部位的分子。这种脂肪信号分子被称为 5-oxoETE，或 5-oxo-6,8,11,14-二十碳四烯酸，当身体需要对威胁做出反应时，它可以充当化学警报。

paras.en: At the time, scientists observed an enzyme that could both produce and break down 5-oxoETE. Enzymes are proteins that help chemical reactions take place, but in this case, researchers could not identify the human gene responsible for making the enzyme.
paras.zh: 当时，科学家观察到一种既能产生又能分解 5-oxoETE 的酶。酶是帮助化学反应发生的蛋白质，但在这种情况下，研究人员无法识别负责制造酶的人类基因。

paras.en: That missing genetic information created a major obstacle. Without knowing which gene produced the enzyme, scientists could not easily manipulate it in experiments or determine how problems with its activity might contribute to disease. Researchers assigned the enzyme a descriptive name based on its chemical function, but its genetic identity remained unknown for more than 30 years.
paras.zh: 缺失的遗传信息造成了一个主要障碍。在不知道哪个基因产生这种酶的情况下，科学家们无法轻易地在实验中操纵它或确定其活性问题如何导致疾病。研究人员根据这种酶的化学功能给它起了一个描述性名称，但 30 多年来，它的遗传身份仍然未知。

paras.en: The breakthrough finally came through the work of Yanan Ma, PhD, a postdoctoral researcher at MSK's Sloan Kettering Institute. Building on earlier investigations by former lab colleague King Lam Hui, PhD, Ma identified the human gene that produces the enzyme, giving researchers a way to examine its function much more closely.
paras.zh: 这一突破最终来自 MSK 斯隆凯特琳研究所博士后研究员 Yanan Ma 博士的工作。在前实验室同事 King Lam Hui 博士早期研究的基础上，Ma 确定了产生这种酶的人类基因，为研究人员提供了一种更仔细地检查其功能的方法。

paras.en: How the Immune System Can Damage Healthy Cells
paras.zh: 免疫系统如何损害健康细胞

paras.en: Ma works in the laboratory of cell biologist Philipp Niethammer, PhD, whose research examines how cells respond to injuries, infections, and other forms of stress. His team focuses on inflammation, tissue repair, and regeneration, biological processes that also play important roles in cancer and numerous other diseases.
paras.zh: 马在细胞生物学家 Philipp Niethammer 博士的实验室工作，他的研究研究细胞如何应对受伤、感染和其他形式的压力。他的团队专注于炎症、组织修复和再生等生物过程，这些生物过程在癌症和许多其他疾病中也发挥着重要作用。

paras.en: When harmful bacteria enter the body, chemical signals help recruit specialized white blood cells to the affected area. One of those signals is 5-oxoETE, which attracts immune cells equipped to attack invading microorganisms.
paras.zh: 当有害细菌进入体内时，化学信号有助于将专门的白细胞招募到受影响的区域。这些信号之一是 5-oxoETE，它会吸引免疫细胞来攻击入侵的微生物。

paras.en: Although this response is essential for fighting infections, it carries risks. The substances immune cells release to destroy pathogens can also injure surrounding healthy tissue.
paras.zh: 尽管这种反应对于对抗感染至关重要，但它也存在风险。免疫细胞释放来消灭病原体的物质也会损伤周围的健康组织。

paras.en: "They flood the site with toxic substances to kill the bacteria," Dr. Niethammer says. "But this can cause damage to healthy cells if it gets out of control."
paras.zh: “他们用有毒物质淹没现场来杀死细菌，”尼特哈默博士说。 “但如果失控，可能会对健康细胞造成损害。”

paras.en: Niethammer's laboratory had already spent years investigating the molecular reactions involved in 5-oxoETE signaling. Researchers were gradually identifying how the different components of the system worked together, but the unknown enzyme remained a major missing piece.
paras.zh: Niethammer 的实验室已经花了数年时间研究 5-oxoETE 信号传导所涉及的分子反应。研究人员逐渐确定了该系统的不同组成部分如何协同工作，但未知的酶仍然是一个主要的缺失部分。

paras.en: Why Zebrafish Succeeded Where Mice Could Not
paras.zh: 为什么斑马鱼能成功而小鼠却不能

paras.en: Most biomedical experiments involving animals use mice or rats because their biological systems share many similarities with humans. However, these familiar laboratory animals had a significant limitation for the question Ma and her colleagues wanted to answer.
paras.zh: 大多数涉及动物的生物医学实验都使用小鼠或大鼠，因为它们的生物系统与人类有许多相似之处。然而，这些熟悉的实验动物对于马和她的同事想要回答的问题有很大的局限性。

paras.en: "Mice and rats are the primary model used in biomedical research," says Dr. Ma, who received a prestigious Marie-Josée Kravis WISE Fellowship in 2023 for her work on the pathway. "It makes sense -- they're mammals, and there's about an 80% overlap between their genes and ours."
paras.zh: “小鼠和大鼠是生物医学研究中使用的主要模型，”马博士说，她因在该途径方面的工作而于 2023 年获得了著名的 Marie-Josée Kravis WISE 奖学金。 “这是有道理的——它们是哺乳动物，它们的基因和我们的基因有大约 80% 的重叠。”

paras.en: Despite those similarities, mice lack a known immune cell receptor capable of recognizing 5-oxoETE. Without that receptor, researchers cannot investigate the complete signaling process in mice.
paras.zh: 尽管有这些相似之处，但小鼠缺乏一种已知的能够识别 5-oxoETE 的免疫细胞受体。如果没有这种受体，研究人员就无法研究小鼠的完整信号传导过程。

paras.en: Zebrafish, however, have retained the necessary biological machinery.
paras.zh: 然而，斑马鱼保留了必要的生物机制。

paras.en: "This means that you can't study the pathway in mice," Dr. Ma says. "But the pathway is intact in fish. So picking the right alternative model was critical to advancing our understanding of how the human body responds."
paras.zh: “这意味着你无法研究小鼠的通路，”马博士说。 “但这条通路在鱼类中是完整的。因此，选择正确的替代模型对于加深我们对人体如何反应的理解至关重要。”

paras.en: Using zebrafish allowed the scientists to explore how the signal operates in a living organism and eventually helped reveal a function that had gone unnoticed for decades.
paras.zh: 利用斑马鱼，科学家们能够探索信号在生物体中的运作方式，并最终帮助揭示了几十年来未被注意到的功能。

paras.en: Scientists Finally Identify the Missing Enzyme
paras.zh: 科学家终于鉴定出缺失的酶

paras.en: Before investigating the process in zebrafish, Ma and Hui began searching for the enzyme's genetic origins using cultured human cells.
paras.zh: 在研究斑马鱼的这一过程之前，马和惠开始利用培养的人类细胞寻找这种酶的遗传起源。

paras.en: They selected several genes that might be responsible and systematically switched them off, looking for changes in the enzyme's activity. One candidate produced a decisive result.
paras.zh: 他们选择了几个可能负责的基因，并系统地关闭它们，寻找酶活性的变化。一位候选人取得了决定性的结果。

paras.en: When Ma disabled a gene called DHRS7, the enzyme stopped functioning. The experiment established that DHRS7 was the gene researchers had been searching for since the early 1990s.
paras.zh: 当 Ma 禁用了一个名为 DHRS7 的基因时，这种酶就停止了功能。该实验证实 DHRS7 是研究人员自 20 世纪 90 年代初以来一直在寻找的基因。

paras.en: Additional tests involving the rodent version of the gene showed almost no enzyme activity. That result was consistent with the absence of the 5-oxoETE receptor in mice, suggesting that rodents had lost key functions associated with this signaling system.
paras.zh: 涉及啮齿动物版本的基因的其他测试显示几乎没有酶活性。该结果与小鼠体内 5-oxoETE 受体的缺失相一致，表明啮齿类动物已经丧失了与该信号系统相关的关键功能。

paras.en: Identifying DHRS7 resolved the long-standing mystery. It also connected Ma's research with a separate investigation underway in the same laboratory, led by postdoctoral researcher Miklos Lengyel, MD, PhD.
paras.zh: DHRS7 的识别解决了这个长期存在的谜团。它还将马云的研究与同一实验室正在进行的一项单独调查联系起来，该调查由博士后研究员 Miklos Lengyel 博士领导。

paras.en: "Typically, when you have a paper with two first authors like Yanan and Miklos, there is just one story that two people contributed to equally," Dr. Niethammer says. "But this paper is not like that. In this paper, there are two separate projects led by two different authors that came together as one larger discovery. And I think that's extremely important to note."
paras.zh: “通常情况下，当一篇论文有两位第一作者（例如亚南和米克洛斯）时，只有一个故事是两个人共同贡献的，”尼特哈默博士说。 “但这篇论文不是那样的。在这篇论文中，有两个不同的作者领导的两个独立的项目，它们汇集在一起​​成为一个更大的发现。我认为这一点非常需要注意。”

paras.en: A Surprising Result Turns Expectations Upside Down
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的结果颠覆了人们的期望

paras.en: While Ma investigated the mysterious enzyme, Lengyel was using zebrafish to study colitis, an inflammatory condition affecting the colon. His experiments involved disabling selected genes to understand how they influenced intestinal inflammation.
paras.zh: 当 Ma 研究这种神秘的酶时，Lengyel 正在利用斑马鱼研究结肠炎，这是一种影响结肠的炎症性疾病。他的实验涉及禁用选定的基因，以了解它们如何影响肠道炎症。

paras.en: One experiment produced an especially puzzling outcome.
paras.zh: 一项实验产生了一个特别令人费解的结果。

paras.en: Lengyel removed a gene called hcar1-4 (the zebrafish version of the human gene OXER1). This gene produces the receptor that recognizes 5-oxoETE and allows cells to respond to its signal.
paras.zh: Lengyel 去除了一个名为 hcar1-4 的基因（人类基因 OXER1 的斑马鱼版本）。该基因产生识别 5-oxoETE 的受体，并允许细胞对其信号做出反应。

paras.en: Because 5-oxoETE helps attract immune cells and initiate inflammation, removing its receptor should theoretically weaken that response.
paras.zh: 由于 5-oxoETE 有助于吸引免疫细胞并引发炎症，因此去除其受体理论上应该会削弱这种反应。

paras.en: "So if you remove the receptor that detects the signal, you'd expect less inflammation, not more," Dr. Lengyel says.
paras.zh: “因此，如果你去除检测信号的受体，你会期望炎症减少，而不是更多，”Lengyel 博士说。

paras.en: Instead, the zebrafish developed intestinal inflammation on their own, even though no infection was present.
paras.zh: 相反，即使不存在感染，斑马鱼也会自行出现肠道炎症。

paras.en: The researchers initially considered whether neutrophils, the white blood cells normally recruited by the signal, might be responsible. However, removing those immune cells did not eliminate the inflammation.
paras.zh: 研究人员最初考虑中性粒细胞（通常由信号招募的白细胞）是否可能是造成这种情况的原因。然而，去除这些免疫细胞并不能消除炎症。

paras.en: This unexpected behavior suggested that the 5-oxoETE pathway was doing something much more complicated than simply activating the immune system.
paras.zh: 这种意想不到的行为表明 5-oxoETE 途径正在做一些比简单地激活免疫系统复杂得多的事情。

paras.en: Disabling an Inflammatory Signal Makes Inflammation Worse
paras.zh: 禁用炎症信号会使炎症恶化

paras.en: The connection between the two research projects became clear after Ma identified DHRS7 as the gene responsible for producing the enzyme involved in 5-oxoETE signaling.
paras.zh: 在 Ma 确定 DHRS7 是负责产生参与 5-oxoETE 信号传导的酶的基因后，这两个研究项目之间的联系变得清晰起来。

paras.en: Lengyel then disabled DHRS7 in zebrafish, preventing the production of the enzyme and disrupting the signaling process.
paras.zh: 随后，Lengyel 禁用了斑马鱼中的 DHRS7，从而阻止了酶的产生并扰乱了信号传导过程。

paras.en: Based on the molecule's established role in attracting immune cells, the researchers expected inflammation to decrease. Instead, they observed the same surprising pattern seen when the receptor was removed: inflammation increased.
paras.zh: 基于该分子在吸引免疫细胞方面的既定作用，研究人员预计炎症会减少。相反，他们观察到了受体被移除后相同的令人惊讶的模式：炎症增加。

paras.en: "It made absolutely no sense," Dr. Lengyel says. "I had to prove using several different methods before the rest of the lab was convinced."
paras.zh: “这完全没有意义，”伦吉尔博士说。 “在实验室的其他人被说服之前，我必须使用几种不同的方法来证明。”

paras.en: The findings pointed to a previously unrecognized function. The signaling pathway did not simply help initiate the immune response. It also appeared to prevent unnecessary damage to healthy cells.
paras.zh: 研究结果指出了一个以前未被识别的功能。信号通路不仅仅帮助启动免疫反应。它似乎还可以防止对健康细胞造成不必要的损害。

paras.en: That dual responsibility explained why eliminating the pathway had such an unexpected effect. By disabling the system, scientists had removed not only an inflammatory signal but also an important source of cellular protection.
paras.zh: 这种双重责任解释了为什么消除这条途径会产生如此意想不到的效果。通过禁用该系统，科学家不仅消除了炎症信号，还消除了细胞保护的重要来源。

paras.en: The Immune System's Hidden Protective Shield
paras.zh: 免疫系统隐藏的保护盾

paras.en: Further experiments revealed how this protection works.
paras.zh: 进一步的实验揭示了这种保护是如何发挥作用的。

paras.en: When immune cells attack dangerous microorganisms, they release highly reactive substances that can harm nearby healthy cells. The 5-oxoETE pathway helps tissues withstand this chemical stress, reducing the risk that the body's own defenses will cause unnecessary injury.
paras.zh: 当免疫细胞攻击危险的微生物时，它们会释放出高活性物质，这些物质会伤害附近的健康细胞。 5-oxoETE 途径帮助组织承受这种化学应激，降低人体自身防御造成不必要伤害的风险。

paras.en: "This makes sense when you think about it," Dr. Niethammer says. "These immune cells unleash chemical warfare against a pathogen, and organisms have evolved an elegant way of protecting healthy cells at the same time."
paras.zh: “仔细想想，这是有道理的，”尼特哈默博士说。 “这些免疫细胞对病原体发动化学战，而生物体同时进化出了一种保护健康细胞的优雅方式。”

paras.en: The researchers found that zebrafish intestinal cells became particularly vulnerable when either 5-oxoETE or its Hcar1-4 receptor was missing. Even the normal bacteria living in the intestine produced enough low-level chemical stress to cause problems when this protective system was disabled.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，当 5-oxoETE 或其 Hcar1-4 受体缺失时，斑马鱼肠道细胞变得特别脆弱。当这种保护系统被禁用时，即使是生活在肠道中的正常细菌也会产生足够低水平的化学应激，从而引起问题。

paras.en: The team traced the cellular protection to a group of enzymes known as NUDIX hydrolases. These enzymes help maintain cellular health by removing damaged DNA building blocks before they can interfere with normal biological processes.
paras.zh: 研究小组将细胞保护作用追溯到一组称为 NUDIX 水解酶的酶。这些酶可以在受损的 DNA 构建模块干扰正常生物过程之前将其清除，从而帮助维持细胞健康。

paras.en: Without the protective signaling pathway, intestinal cells could no longer withstand the chemical stress associated with ordinary gut bacteria. Some cells died, setting off an inflammatory response despite the absence of an invading pathogen.
paras.zh: 如果没有保护性信号通路，肠道细胞将无法承受与普通肠道细菌相关的化学应激。尽管没有入侵的病原体，但一些细胞死亡，引发炎症反应。

paras.en: The results revealed that the body uses the same molecular system both to call immune cells into action and to protect healthy tissue from the consequences.
paras.zh: 结果表明，人体使用相同的分子系统来调用免疫细胞发挥作用并保护健康组织免受后果影响。

paras.en: "As it turns out, this signal isn't just an alarm, it's also a shield," Dr. Niethammer says.
paras.zh: “事实证明，这个信号不仅仅是一个警报，它也是一个盾牌，”尼特哈默博士说。

paras.en: Potential Implications for Cancer and Inflammatory Diseases
paras.zh: 对癌症和炎症疾病的潜在影响

paras.en: Understanding this protective mechanism could have important implications for diseases involving excessive or poorly controlled inflammation.
paras.zh: 了解这种保护机制可能对涉及过度或控制不良炎症的疾病具有重要意义。

paras.en: The 5-oxoETE signaling pathway is known to be disrupted in conditions such as cancer, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and asthma. By identifying its previously unknown protective role, researchers have gained a new perspective on how those disruptions might contribute to tissue damage.
paras.zh: 已知 5-oxoETE 信号通路在癌症、炎症性肠病 (IBD) 和哮喘等疾病中会受到破坏。通过确定其以前未知的保护作用，研究人员对这些破坏如何导致组织损伤有了新的认识。

paras.en: In human cancers, mutations affecting DHRS7 and OXER1 (the human version of hcar1-4) have been identified in tumors of the gastrointestinal tract and uterus.
paras.zh: 在人类癌症中，已在胃肠道和子宫肿瘤中发现了影响 DHRS7 和 OXER1（hcar1-4 的人类版本）的突变。

paras.en: Research has also linked mutations that prevent OXER1 from functioning properly with poorer outcomes in patients with colorectal, pancreatic, and kidney cancers.
paras.zh: 研究还发现，阻止 OXER1 正常发挥作用的突变与结直肠癌、胰腺癌和肾癌患者的较差预后有关。

paras.en: The findings suggest that strengthening the pathway might eventually help healthy tissues tolerate damaging conditions more effectively. One possible application involves protecting the intestine from oxidative stress associated with cancer treatment.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，加强该途径可能最终有助于健康组织更有效地耐受破坏性条件。一种可能的应用涉及保护肠道免受与癌症治疗相关的氧化应激。

paras.en: "More research is needed, but there's a possibility that activating the pathway could increase the resilience of the gut to oxidative stress -- which might help counteract damage caused by radiation therapy or chemotherapy," Dr. Lengyel says.
paras.zh: “还需要更多的研究，但激活该途径有可能增加肠道对氧化应激的抵抗力，这可能有助于抵消放射治疗或化疗造成的损伤，”Lengyel 博士说。

paras.en: The discovery also has implications for diseases affecting mucosal tissues, the protective linings found in areas such as the intestines and respiratory tract.
paras.zh: 这一发现还对影响粘膜组织的疾病产生了影响，粘膜组织是肠道和呼吸道等区域的保护层。

paras.en: In people with IBD, researchers have previously associated lower concentrations of 5-oxoETE in intestinal tissue with worse disease outcomes.
paras.zh: 对于 IBD 患者，研究人员此前已将肠道组织中 5-oxoETE 浓度较低与较差的疾病结果联系起来。

paras.en: Evidence from asthma research points to another possible protective function. An independent study involving primates found that blocking OXER1 weakened the immune cell response but also caused protective mucus-producing cells in the airways to disappear.
paras.zh: 哮喘研究的证据指出了另一种可能的保护功能。一项涉及灵长类动物的独立研究发现，阻断 OXER1 会削弱免疫细胞反应，但也会导致气道中产生保护性粘液的细胞消失。

paras.en: Together, these observations suggest that attempts to suppress inflammation must account for the protective roles certain inflammatory signals perform. However, further research will be necessary to determine whether targeting this pathway can produce safe and effective treatments in humans.
paras.zh: 总之，这些观察结果表明，抑制炎症的尝试必须考虑到某些炎症信号所发挥的保护作用。然而，还需要进一步的研究来确定针对这一途径是否可以对人类产生安全有效的治疗方法。

paras.en: How Physical Injury Activates the Same Defense System
paras.zh: 身体伤害如何激活相同的防御系统

paras.en: The researchers are also investigating how this signaling pathway responds to physical damage, not just infection or chemical stress.
paras.zh: 研究人员还在研究该信号通路如何响应物理损伤，而不仅仅是感染或化学应激。

paras.en: That aspect of the work is being explored by doctoral student Zaza Gelashvili, MS, who studies how cells detect mechanical forces associated with tissue injury.
paras.zh: 博士生 Zaza Gelashvili（理学硕士）正在探索这方面的工作，他研究细胞如何检测与组织损伤相关的机械力。

paras.en: When cells experience physical stress, changes to their membranes can initiate the same chain of molecular reactions involved in inflammation.
paras.zh: 当细胞经历物理压力时，细胞膜的变化会引发与炎症相关的相同分子反应链。

paras.en: One early step occurs when stressed cell membranes release arachidonic acid, a fatty molecule that serves as the starting material for producing 5-oxoETE.
paras.zh: 当受压的细胞膜释放花生四烯酸时，就会发生一个早期步骤，花生四烯酸是一种脂肪分子，可作为生产 5-oxoETE 的起始材料。

paras.en: Gelashvili, a co-author of the Nature study, led a separate investigation into the molecular signals associated with physical wounds. That research was published in Nature Communications earlier in 2026. His contributions were also recognized with the 2026 Chairman's Prize from the Gerstner Sloan Kettering Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences.
paras.zh: 《自然》研究的合著者格拉什维利领导了一项针对与身体伤口相关的分子信号的单独研究。该研究于 2026 年初发表在《自然通讯》上。他的贡献还获得了格斯特纳·斯隆·凯特林生物医学科学研究生院颁发的 2026 年主席奖的认可。

paras.en: "There's a mechanical component to the pathway that's upstream of what Yanan and Miklos have been studying," explains Gelashvili, a co-author on the study who led a separate study on physical wound signals that was published in Nature Communications earlier this year; his work was also recognized with the 2026 Chairman's Prize from the Gerstner Sloan Kettering Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences. "You can think of it as the first step in a chain reaction: Physical stress unlocks the raw material, oxidative stress drives the conversion, and DHRS7 amplifies the signal."
paras.zh: 该研究的合著者 Gelashvili 解释说：“该通路中有一个机械成分，位于 Yanan 和 Miklos 一直在研究的上游。”Gelashvili 领导了一项关于物理伤口信号的单独研究，该研究于今年早些时候发表在《自然通讯》上。他的工作还获得了格斯特纳·斯隆·凯特林生物医学科学研究生院颁发的 2026 年主席奖。 “你可以将其视为连锁反应的第一步：物理压力释放原材料，氧化压力驱动转化，DHRS7 放大信号。”

paras.en: The research suggests that the body combines information about different forms of cellular stress to coordinate its response. Physical damage can initiate the process, chemical stress can influence the conversion of signaling molecules, and DHRS7 helps strengthen the resulting signal.
paras.zh: 研究表明，身体结合了不同形式的细胞压力的信息来协调其反应。物理损伤可以启动该过程，化学应激可以影响信号分子的转换，而 DHRS7 有助于增强产生的信号。

paras.en: Rather than operating as separate responses, these processes appear to work together to help the body recognize danger while limiting unnecessary harm to healthy cells.
paras.zh: 这些过程并不是单独的反应，而是协同作用，帮助身体识别危险，同时限制对健康细胞的不必要伤害。

paras.en: "What we are really studying is a pathway that integrates two completely different kinds of stress -- mechanical and metabolic -- and converts them into a single, coordinated, protective response," Dr. Niethammer says.
paras.zh: “我们真正研究的是一种整合两种完全不同的压力——机械压力和代谢压力——并将它们转化为单一、协调的保护性反应的途径，”尼特哈默博士说。

paras.en: Additional researchers contributing to the study were Yohannes Ambaw, Leehyeon Kim, Ritchie Ly, Siyang Peng, Meysoon Quraishi, Tobias Walther, and Robert Farese Jr., all affiliated with MSK.
paras.zh: 参与这项研究的其他研究人员包括 Yohannes Ambaw、Leehyeon Kim、Ritchie Ly、Siyang Peng、Meysoon Quraishi、Tobias Walther 和 Robert Farese Jr.，他们都隶属于 MSK。

paras.en: Financial support came from the National Institutes of Health (R35GM140883); an MSK Basic Research Innovation Award; a Starr Foundation Program for Discovery Science grant; a Tow Foundation fellowship; a Marie-Josée Kravis Women in Science Endeavor (WISE) fellowship; a Crohn's Colitis Foundation Research Fellows Award (1268111); an Experimental Immuno-Oncology Scholars fellowship; and core facility services supported in part by MSK's National Cancer Institute Cancer Center Support grant (P30CA008748).
paras.zh: 财政支持来自美国国立卫生研究院 (R35GM140883)； MSK 斯隆基础研究创新奖；斯塔尔基金会发现科学资助计划；陶尔基金会奖学金； Marie-Josée Kravis 女性科学奋进 (WISE) 奖学金；克罗恩病结肠炎基金会研究员奖（1268111）；实验免疫肿瘤学学者奖学金；核心设施服务部分由 MSK 斯隆国家癌症研究所癌症中心支持赠款 (P30CA008748) 提供支持。

paras.zh: 材料由纪念斯隆凯特琳癌症中心提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

Farese, Philipp Niethammer. 5-oxoETE links redox control of epithelial damage detection and resilience. Nature, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11121-2

articles.title: Goodbye, cavities? Scientists create gel that could regrow tooth enamel

paras.en: Goodbye, cavities? Scientists create gel that could regrow tooth enamel
paras.zh: 再见，蛀牙？科学家研制出可以再生牙釉质的凝胶

paras.en: - Scientists have developed a revolutionary gel that could regrow lost tooth enamel by harnessing minerals naturally found in saliva, potentially overcoming one of dentistryâs biggest limitations. The regenerated enamel behaves much like healthy enamel, raising hopes for a simple treatment that could repair damaged teeth, prevent decay, and reduce sensitivity.
paras.zh: - 科学家们开发出了一种革命性的凝胶，可以通过利用唾液中天然存在的矿物质来重新生长丢失的牙釉质，从而有可能克服牙科的最大限制之一。再生的牙釉质的行为与健康的牙釉质非常相似，这让人们对一种可以修复受损牙齿、防止腐烂和降低敏感性的简单治疗方法产生了希望。

paras.en: Scientists have developed a new gel that could make it possible to regrow damaged tooth enamel, potentially overcoming one of the biggest limitations in dental care. Unlike bones and many other tissues in the body, tooth enamel cannot naturally regenerate once it has been lost. The new treatment offers a promising way to rebuild this protective layer, strengthen teeth, and help prevent future decay.
paras.zh: 科学家们开发出了一种新的凝胶，可以使受损的牙釉质再生，从而有可能克服牙科护理的最大限制之一。与骨骼和体内许多其他组织不同，牙釉质一旦丢失就无法自然再生。新的治疗方法提供了一种重建保护层、强化牙齿并帮助防止未来腐烂的有前途的方法。

paras.en: The innovation comes from researchers at the University of Nottingham's School of Pharmacy and Department of Chemical and Environmental Engineering. Their new material is inspired by the biological processes that form tooth enamel during early childhood. It is designed to repair enamel that has been weakened by mineral loss or worn away by erosion, while also reinforcing enamel that remains healthy.
paras.zh: 这项创新来自诺丁汉大学药学院和化学与环境工程系的研究人员。他们的新材料的灵感来自于幼儿时期形成牙釉质的生物过程。它旨在修复因矿物质流失而削弱或因侵蚀而磨损的牙釉质，同时强化保持健康的牙釉质。

paras.en: The findings, published in Nature Communications, could pave the way for a new generation of dental treatments that go beyond protecting existing enamel and actually help restore its structure.
paras.zh: 这项发表在《自然通讯》上的研究结果可能为新一代牙科治疗铺平道路，这种治疗不仅限于保护现有的牙釉质，而且实际上有助于恢复其结构。

paras.en: One of the most promising features of the technology is its simplicity. Dentists could apply the gel directly to teeth using a procedure similar to existing fluoride treatments, making it potentially easy to incorporate into routine dental care.
paras.zh: 该技术最有前途的特点之一是它的简单性。牙医可以使用类似于现有氟化物治疗的程序将凝胶直接涂抹在牙齿上，从而可以轻松地将其纳入常规牙科护理中。

paras.en: Unlike conventional fluoride products, however, the new gel contains no fluoride. Instead, it uses a material made from proteins that imitates important characteristics of the natural proteins responsible for guiding enamel formation when teeth first develop.
paras.zh: 然而，与传统的氟化物产品不同，新型凝胶不含氟化物。相反，它使用由蛋白质制成的材料，模仿天然蛋白质的重要​​特征，该蛋白质负责在牙齿首次发育时引导牙釉质形成。

paras.en: Once applied, the gel forms a thin but durable coating that penetrates the tooth's surface and fills microscopic cracks and gaps. This coating then provides a framework for rebuilding the mineral structure of enamel.
paras.zh: 一旦涂抹，凝胶就会形成一层薄而耐用的涂层，渗透牙齿表面并填充微小的裂缝和间隙。然后，该涂层提供了重建牙釉质矿物结构的框架。

paras.en: The process relies on calcium and phosphate ions, two essential mineral components naturally present in saliva. The gel attracts these minerals and helps organize them into new crystals that grow in an orderly pattern.
paras.zh: 该过程依赖于钙离子和磷酸盐离子，这是唾液中天然存在的两种重要矿物质成分。凝胶吸引这些矿物质并帮助它们组织成新的晶体，并以有序的方式生长。

paras.en: Scientists call this process epitaxial mineralization. Essentially, it means that new mineral crystals grow in alignment with the existing enamel, allowing the newly formed material to become structurally integrated with the original tooth surface.
paras.zh: 科学家将这个过程称为外延矿化。从本质上讲，这意味着新的矿物晶体与现有的牙釉质对齐生长，使新形成的材料在结构上与原始牙齿表面融为一体。

paras.en: This organization is especially important because enamel gets its exceptional hardness and durability from the precise arrangement of its mineral crystals. Simply depositing minerals on a tooth is not enough to recreate the complex structure that makes natural enamel so effective.
paras.zh: 这种组织尤其重要，因为牙釉质因其矿物晶体的精确排列而具有卓越的硬度和耐用性。仅仅将矿物质沉积在牙齿上不足以重建使天然牙釉质如此有效的复杂结构。

paras.en: By guiding crystal growth, the new gel can restore both the microscopic architecture and the physical properties of healthy enamel.
paras.zh: 通过引导晶体生长，新型凝胶可以恢复健康牙釉质的微观结构和物理特性。

paras.en: A Potential Solution for Tooth Sensitivity and Decay
paras.zh: 牙齿敏感和蛀牙的潜在解决方案

paras.en: The researchers also discovered that their material can be used on exposed dentine, commonly called dentin in the United States. Dentin is the layer of tooth tissue beneath the enamel. It is softer than enamel and contains tiny channels that can transmit sensations toward the nerves inside the tooth.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现他们的材料可以用于暴露的牙本质，在美国通常称为牙本质。牙本质是牙釉质下方的牙齿组织层。它比牙釉质更柔软，并且含有微小的通道，可以将感觉传递到牙齿内部的神经。

paras.en: When enamel wears away, or gums recede, exposed dentin can make teeth particularly sensitive to hot, cold, sweet, or acidic foods and drinks.
paras.zh: 当牙釉质磨损或牙龈退缩时，暴露的牙本质会使牙齿对热、冷、甜或酸性食物和饮料特别敏感。

paras.en: The new gel can encourage the formation of an enamel-like mineral layer over exposed dentin. This could help reduce tooth sensitivity while also improving the attachment of dental restorations, such as fillings and other treatments used to repair damaged teeth.
paras.zh: 新的凝胶可以促进在暴露的牙本质上形成牙釉质矿物质层。这可以帮助降低牙齿敏感性，同时还可以改善牙齿修复体的附着力，例如填充物和用于修复受损牙齿的其他治疗方法。

paras.en: The potential benefits are significant. Enamel deterioration is a major factor in tooth decay and contributes to dental problems that affect nearly half of the world's population. These conditions can cause pain, infections, and eventually tooth loss. Poor oral health is also associated with broader health problems, including diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
paras.zh: 潜在的好处是巨大的。牙釉质恶化是蛀牙的一个主要因素，并导致影响世界近一半人口的牙齿问题。这些情况会导致疼痛、感染，并最终导致牙齿脱落。口腔健康状况不佳还与更广泛的健康问题有关，包括糖尿病和心血管疾病。

paras.en: One of the greatest challenges in dentistry is that enamel has no living cells capable of rebuilding it after teeth have fully developed. Although saliva can naturally replace some minerals lost during the earliest stages of enamel damage, the body cannot regenerate substantial amounts of enamel that have been worn away.
paras.zh: 牙科面临的最大挑战之一是牙釉质没有能够在牙齿完全发育后重建的活细胞。尽管唾液可以自然地替代牙釉质损坏早期阶段损失的一些矿物质，但身体无法再生大量磨损的牙釉质。

paras.en: Existing treatments, including fluoride varnishes and remineralization products, can help protect teeth and repair early mineral loss. However, they cannot fully reconstruct enamel that has already been lost.
paras.zh: 现有的治疗方法，包括氟化物清漆和再矿​​化产品，可以帮助保护牙齿并修复早期矿物质流失。然而，他们无法完全重建已经丢失的牙釉质。

paras.en: The new technology aims to overcome that limitation by encouraging the formation of new mineral tissue with properties resembling those of the original enamel.
paras.zh: 这项新技术旨在通过促进具有与原始牙釉质相似特性的新矿物组织的形成来克服这一限制。

paras.en: Regenerated Enamel Performs Like Natural Tooth Enamel
paras.zh: 再生牙釉质的性能与天然牙釉质相似

paras.en: The research team tested the mechanical strength and durability of the regenerated material under conditions designed to mimic everyday use.
paras.zh: 研究小组在模拟日常使用的条件下测试了再生材料的机械强度和耐久性。

paras.en: These experiments examined how the newly formed enamel responded to activities and exposures that teeth routinely experience, including brushing, chewing, and contact with acidic foods.
paras.zh: 这些实验检查了新形成的牙釉质如何响应牙齿日常活动和暴露，包括刷牙、咀嚼和接触酸性食物。

paras.en: The results were encouraging. According to the researchers, the regenerated enamel displayed mechanical properties comparable to those of healthy natural enamel, suggesting that the material could provide more than a temporary protective coating.
paras.zh: 结果令人鼓舞。研究人员表示，再生牙釉质显示出与健康天然牙釉质相当的机械性能，这表明该材料可以提供的不仅仅是临时保护涂层。

paras.en: Dr. Abshar Hasan, a postdoctoral fellow and the study's lead author, explained why recreating enamel's internal structure is so important.
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、博士后研究员 Abshar Hasan 博士解释了为什么重建牙釉质的内部结构如此重要。

paras.en: "Dental enamel has a unique structure, which gives enamel its remarkable properties that protect our teeth throughout life against physical, chemical, and thermal insults. When our material is applied to demineralized or eroded enamel, or exposed dentine, the material promotes the growth of crystals in an integrated and organized manner, recovering the architecture of our natural healthy enamel. We have tested the mechanical properties of these regenerated tissues under conditions simulating 'real-life situations' such as tooth brushing, chewing, and exposure to acidic foods, and found that the regenerated enamel behaves just like healthy enamel."
paras.zh: “牙釉质具有独特的结构，赋予牙釉质非凡的特性，可以在整个生命过程中保护我们的牙齿免受物理、化学和热损伤。当我们的材料应用于脱矿或侵蚀的牙釉质或暴露的牙本质时，该材料会以集成和有组织的方式促进晶体生长，恢复我们天然健康牙釉质的结构。我们在模拟“现实生活情况”的条件下测试了这些再生组织的机械性能，例如刷牙、刷牙、咀嚼和接触酸性食物，发现再生的牙釉质表现得就像健康的牙釉质一样。”

paras.en: These findings suggest that the gel could eventually offer a way to restore the strength and protective function of damaged enamel rather than simply slowing further deterioration. However, the laboratory results do not yet establish how well the treatment will perform over extended periods in patients.
paras.zh: 这些发现表明，凝胶最终可以提供一种恢复受损牙釉质的强度和保护功能的方法，而不是简单地减缓进一步恶化。然而，实验室结果尚未确定这种治疗在患者身上的长期效果如何。

paras.en: Beyond its ability to regenerate enamel, the researchers emphasize that the technology was developed with practical dental applications in mind.
paras.zh: 除了再生牙釉质的能力之外，研究人员强调，该技术的开发还考虑到了牙科的实际应用。

paras.en: The gel is designed to be safe, simple to apply, and suitable for manufacturing on a larger scale. Its versatility could also allow it to be incorporated into several types of dental products, potentially benefiting patients of different ages with enamel erosion, tooth sensitivity, or other problems involving exposed dentin.
paras.zh: 该凝胶的设计安全、使用简单，并且适合大规模生产。它的多功能性还可以使其融入多种类型的牙科产品中，从而可能使患有牙釉质侵蚀、牙齿敏感或涉及牙本质暴露的其他问题的不同年龄的患者受益。

paras.en: Professor Alvaro Mata, Chair in Biomedical Engineering & Biomaterials at the University of Nottingham, led the study and highlighted the potential for translating the discovery into products that dentists can use.
paras.zh: 诺丁汉大学生物医学工程与生物材料系主任阿尔瓦罗·马塔教授领导了这项研究，并强调了将这一发现转化为牙医可以使用的产品的潜力。

paras.en: "We are very excited because the technology has been designed with the clinician and patient in mind. It is safe, can be easily and rapidly applied, and it is scalable. Also, the technology is versatile, which opens the opportunity to be translated into multiple types of products to help patients of all ages suffering from a variety of dental problems associated with loss of enamel and exposed dentine. We have started this process with our start-up company Mintech-Bio and hope to have a first product out by next year; this innovation could soon be helping patients worldwide."
paras.zh: “我们非常兴奋，因为该技术的设计考虑了临床医生和患者的需求。它安全，可以轻松快速地应用，并且具有可扩展性。此外，该技术具有多功能性，这为转化为多种类型的产品提供了机会，以帮助所有年龄段的患者，帮助患有与牙釉质损失和牙本质暴露相关的各种牙科问题的患者。我们已经与初创公司 Mintech-Bio 开始了这一过程，并希望在明年推出第一个产品；这项创新很快就会帮助全世界的患者。”

paras.en: The researchers have already begun working toward commercialization through their company, Mintech-Bio, with the goal of introducing an initial product as early as the year following the announcement.
paras.zh: 研究人员已经开始通过他们的公司 Mintech-Bio 致力于商业化，目标是最早在宣布后的第二年推出初始产品。

paras.en: Although further development and clinical validation will be important before the technology becomes an established dental treatment, its ability to recreate the structure and strength of natural enamel represents a promising advance.
paras.zh: 尽管在该技术成为成熟的牙科治疗方法之前，进一步的开发和临床验证非常重要，但其重建天然牙釉质结构和强度的能力代表了一个有希望的进步。

paras.en: If the approach proves successful in patients, it could fundamentally change how dentists address enamel loss, opening the possibility of rebuilding tooth surfaces that previously could only be protected or restored using conventional dental materials.
paras.zh: 如果这种方法在患者身上证明是成功的，它可能会从根本上改变牙医解决牙釉质损失的方式，从而为重建以前只能使用传统牙科材料保护或修复的牙齿表面提供了可能性。

articles.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss

paras.en: Scientists discover mysterious âlonelyâ brain waves linked to memory loss
paras.zh: 科学家发现神秘的“孤独”脑电波与记忆丧失有关

paras.en: - Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between Alzheimerâs-related protein buildup, disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, and fading memory. The findings suggest that hidden changes in how the brain processes memories overnight may contribute to age-related memory loss long before Alzheimerâs symptoms appear.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了与阿尔茨海默氏症相关的蛋白质堆积、深度睡眠期间脑电波紊乱和记忆力衰退之间存在令人惊讶的联系。研究结果表明，早在阿尔茨海默病症状出现之前，大脑在一夜之间处理记忆的隐藏变化可能会导致与年龄相关的记忆丧失。

paras.en: You walk out of the grocery store, ready to head home and make dinner. But as you scan the crowded parking lot, a frustrating question comes to mind. Where did you leave your car? You try to picture the spot, but the memory refuses to surface.
paras.zh: 你走出杂货店，准备回家做晚饭。但当你扫视拥挤的停车场时，你的脑海中浮现出一个令人沮丧的问题。你把车停在哪里了？你试图想象那个地点，但记忆却无法浮现出来。

paras.en: Remembering personal experiences like these depends on episodic memory, which allows us to recall events from our lives. These memories help form the foundation of long-term memory, whether they involve a childhood milestone, such as the first day of elementary school, or something that happened just minutes earlier, like parking your car.
paras.zh: 记住这些个人经历​​取决于情景记忆，它使我们能够回忆起生活中的事件。这些记忆有助于形成长期记忆的基础，无论它们涉及童年的里程碑，例如小学的第一天，还是几分钟前发生的事情，例如停车。

paras.en: This ability tends to weaken as we grow older. The sights, sounds, and other details associated with past experiences can become increasingly difficult to retrieve. Scientists still do not fully understand why this happens. Although some memory decline is a common part of aging, the changes can become far more severe in people developing Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 随着年龄的增长，这种能力往往会减弱。与过去的经历相关的景象、声音和其他细节可能变得越来越难以检索。科学家们仍然不完全明白为什么会发生这种情况。尽管记忆力下降是衰老的常见现象，但对于患有阿尔茨海默病的人来说，这种变化可能会变得更加严重。

paras.en: A new study from researchers at the University of California, Berkeley, offers important clues about what may be happening inside the aging brain. Neuroscientist Omer Sharon and his colleagues, working under the direction of former Berkeley sleep researcher Matthew Walker, discovered a connection between disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, declining memory performance, and the accumulation of tau, a protein associated with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校研究人员的一项新研究提供了有关衰老大脑内部可能发生的情况的重要线索。神经科学家 Omer Sharon 和他的同事在前伯克利睡眠研究员 Matthew Walker 的指导下，发现深度睡眠期间脑电波紊乱、记忆力下降以及 tau 蛋白（一种与阿尔茨海默病相关的蛋白质）积累之间存在联系。

paras.en: The findings suggest that tau buildup in the brain's frontal cortex is linked to changes in the coordinated electrical activity that helps preserve memories overnight.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，大脑额叶皮层中 tau 蛋白的积累与协调电活动的变化有关，而协调电活动有助于在一夜之间保存记忆。

paras.en: "This is the first time we've shown this relationship between tau and how it messes with memory consolidation by attenuating traveling slow waves that originate in the frontal cortex," said Sharon, a postdoctoral researcher at UC Berkeley's Center for Human Sleep Science.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校人类睡眠科学中心的博士后研究员 Sharon 说：“这是我们第一次证明 tau 蛋白与它如何通过减弱源自额叶皮层的慢波来扰乱记忆巩固之间的关系。”

paras.en: The research was published in Nature Neuroscience.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《自然神经科学》杂志上。

paras.en: How Deep Sleep Helps the Brain Store Memories
paras.zh: 深度睡眠如何帮助大脑存储记忆

paras.en: Sleep involves several distinct stages, each associated with different patterns of brain activity. Rapid eye movement sleep is particularly recognizable because the eyes move beneath closed eyelids and most dreaming takes place during this stage. However, another stage, known as non-REM sleep, is especially important for maintaining healthy brain function.
paras.zh: 睡眠涉及几个不同的阶段，每个阶段都与不同的大脑活动模式相关。快速眼动睡眠特别容易识别，因为眼睛在闭合的眼睑下方移动，并且大多数梦发生在这个阶段。然而，另一个阶段，即非快速眼动睡眠，对于维持健康的大脑功能尤其重要。

paras.en: During this deeper stage of sleep, when dreaming is limited or absent, large groups of neurons briefly become inactive and then active again in a coordinated sequence. These synchronized changes produce slow electrical waves that spread across the brain, typically beginning in the frontal cortex.
paras.zh: 在这个更深的睡眠阶段，当做梦受到限制或不存在时，大群神经元会短暂地变得不活跃，然后以协调的顺序再次活跃。这些同步变化会产生缓慢的电波，并在整个大脑中传播，通常从额叶皮层开始。

paras.en: "Each slow wave reflects an enormous population of neurons switching off and back on together," Sharon said. "Our study shows that for memory, it's critical that these events cascade in sequence across large parts of the brain. This coordinated shutdown has been observed only during deep sleep, and may be one reason why we sleep."
paras.zh: 莎伦说：“每个慢波都反映出大量神经元同时关闭和重新打开。” “我们的研究表明，对于记忆来说，这些事件在大脑的大部分区域按顺序级联是至关重要的。只有在深度睡眠期间才能观察到这种协调的关闭，这可能是我们睡觉的原因之一。”

paras.en: The researchers found that this carefully organized activity becomes less coordinated as tau accumulates in the aging brain. Instead of traveling together across broad regions, the waves become more scattered and cover shorter distances. These changes are associated with weaker memory consolidation, declining cognitive abilities, and Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，随着 tau 蛋白在衰老大脑中积累，这种精心组织的活动变得不那么协调。这些波不再一起穿过广阔的区域，而是变得更加分散，覆盖的距离也更短。这些变化与记忆巩固减弱、认知能力下降和阿尔茨海默病有关。

paras.en: Alzheimer's Protein Linked to Disrupted Brain Waves
paras.zh: 阿尔茨海默氏症蛋白质与脑电波紊乱有关

paras.en: To investigate the relationship, the scientists monitored sleeping brain activity using electroencephalograms (EEGs). They compared cognitively healthy young adults in their early 20s with older participants ranging from their mid-60s to mid-70s.
paras.zh: 为了研究这种关系，科学家们使用脑电图（EEG）监测睡眠时的大脑活动。他们将 20 岁出头认知健康的年轻人与 60 多岁到 70 多岁的老年参与者进行了比较。

paras.en: The differences were striking. In younger participants, groups of slow waves moved together across distances roughly equivalent to the width of a hand on the scalp. Among older adults, the waves typically traveled less far and appeared more independently, rather than moving in coordinated groups.
paras.zh: The differences were striking.在年轻的参与者中，慢波组一起移动的距离大致相当于手掌在头皮上的宽度。在老年人中，波浪通常传播的距离较短，并且显得更加独立，而不是以协调的群体移动。

paras.en: The team also examined whether these changes were associated with tau accumulation. Working with Dr. William Jagust, a UC Berkeley professor emeritus of public health and neuroscience, the researchers used positron emission tomography (PET) scans to examine the brains of older participants. This imaging technique uses radioactive tracers introduced into the bloodstream to reveal biological activity and the distribution of specific substances.
paras.zh: 研究小组还检查了这些变化是否与 tau 蛋白积累有关。研究人员与加州大学伯克利分校公共卫生和神经科学名誉教授 William Jagust 博士合作，使用正电子发射断层扫描 (PET) 扫描来检查老年参与者的大脑。这种成像技术使用引入血液的放射性示踪剂来揭示生物活性和特定物质的分布。

paras.en: The scans showed that greater tau buildup in the frontal cortex was associated with a breakdown in the longer traveling waves normally seen during deep sleep.
paras.zh: 扫描结果显示，额叶皮层中 tau 蛋白的堆积与深度睡眠期间通常出现的较长行波的崩溃有关。

paras.en: Importantly, these changes were present in people who had not developed Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 重要的是，这些变化也出现在未患阿尔茨海默病的人身上。

paras.en: "These people did not have Alzheimer's," Sharon said. "They had tau in their brains, but with subclinical impacts. Their memory decline was within the normal range for their age."
paras.zh: “这些人没有患有阿尔茨海默氏症，”莎伦说。 “他们的大脑中含有 tau 蛋白，但具有亚临床影响。他们的记忆力下降在其年龄的正常范围内。”

paras.en: Sharon explained that early Alzheimer's related changes can vary considerably in severity. The amount of tau present in the brain is associated with cognitive performance, even when a person's memory abilities remain within the expected range for their age.
paras.zh: 莎伦解释说，早期阿尔茨海默病相关的变化的严重程度可能有很大差异。即使一个人的记忆能力保持在其年龄的预期范围内，大脑中存在的 tau 蛋白含量也与认知能力相关。

paras.en: Mysterious "Lonely Waves" Linked to Memory Loss
paras.zh: 神秘的“孤独波浪”与记忆丧失有关

paras.en: The researchers wanted to determine whether the altered sleep patterns were associated with actual differences in how well people remembered information.
paras.zh: 研究人员想要确定睡眠模式的改变是否与人们记忆信息的实际差异有关。

paras.en: To test this, participants learned pairs of associated words in the evening. The following day, they were asked to recall what they had learned, allowing the scientists to evaluate how effectively the memories had been retained overnight.
paras.zh: 为了测试这一点，参与者在晚上学习了成对的关联词。第二天，他们被要求回忆所学内容，以便科学家评估记忆在一夜之间保留的效果。

paras.en: Participants whose slow brain waves traveled shorter distances and appeared more isolated generally remembered fewer word associations. The researchers called these disconnected patterns "lonely waves."
paras.zh: 脑电波缓慢的参与者的传播距离较短且显得更加孤立，通常记住的单词联想较少。研究人员将这些不连贯的模式称为“孤独波”。

paras.en: The team also tracked a subset of participants over several years to see how their brains changed with time. Among those whose frontal cortex tau levels increased, the slow waves became less coordinated, and their ability to retain newly learned information overnight declined.
paras.zh: 该团队还对一部分参与者进行了数年追踪，以了解他们的大脑如何随时间变化。在那些额叶皮层tau蛋白水平增加的人中，慢波变得不那么协调，他们在一夜之间保留新学到的信息的能力下降了。

paras.en: These observations provide evidence of a relationship between tau accumulation, changes in deep sleep brain activity, and worsening episodic memory. However, they do not establish that tau buildup directly causes memory loss or that disrupted waves are the mechanism responsible.
paras.zh: 这些观察结果提供了 tau 蛋白积累、深度睡眠大脑活动变化和情景记忆恶化之间关系的证据。然而，他们并没有证实 tau 蛋白的积累会直接导致记忆丧失，也没有证实波的破坏是造成这种现象的机制。

paras.en: Additional Tests Strengthen the Connection
paras.zh: 额外的测试加强连接

paras.en: Because PET scans are costly and require specialized facilities, the scientists sought another way to investigate the relationship between Alzheimer's related proteins and sleep activity.
paras.zh: 由于 PET 扫描成本高昂且需要专门的设施，因此科学家们寻求另一种方法来研究阿尔茨海默病相关蛋白质与睡眠活动之间的关系。

paras.en: They collaborated with neurologist Yo-El Ju at Washington University in St. Louis to analyze spinal fluid from a separate group of older adults. The goal was to determine whether measurements of Alzheimer's associated proteins would reveal patterns similar to those seen with brain imaging.
paras.zh: 他们与圣路易斯华盛顿大学的神经学家 Yo-El Ju 合作，分析了另一组老年人的脊髓液。目标是确定阿尔茨海默病相关蛋白质的测量是否会揭示与大脑成像相似的模式。

paras.en: Unlike PET scans, the spinal fluid measurements could not identify tau accumulation specifically within the frontal cortex. Nevertheless, the results pointed in the same direction.
paras.zh: 与 PET 扫描不同，脊髓液测量无法识别额叶皮层内的 tau 蛋白积聚。尽管如此，结果还是指向了同一个方向。

paras.en: People whose sleeping brains produced more isolated slow waves had higher ratios of tau to amyloid, another protein closely associated with Alzheimer's disease, in their spinal fluid.
paras.zh: 睡眠中大脑产生更多孤立慢波的人，其脊髓液中 tau 蛋白与淀粉样蛋白（另一种与阿尔茨海默病密切相关的蛋白质）的比例较高。

paras.en: The consistency between these independent groups and testing methods strengthened the researchers' confidence in the findings.
paras.zh: 这些独立群体和测试方法之间的一致性增强了研究人员对研究结果的信心。

paras.en: "It's collected in a totally different place and in a different cohort, so I think that adds to the strength of the evidence," Sharon said.
paras.zh: “它是在完全不同的地方和不同的人群中收集的，所以我认为这增加了证据的强度，”莎伦说。

paras.en: Together, the sleep recordings, brain scans, spinal fluid analyses, and memory assessments suggest that tau accumulation is associated with a particular disruption of brain activity during deep sleep.
paras.zh: 睡眠记录、脑部扫描、脊髓液分析和记忆评估共同表明，tau 蛋白的积累与深度睡眠期间大脑活动的特定破坏有关。

paras.en: "This longitudinal correlation suggests that Alzheimer's disease pathology is associated with a disruption of this main sleep feature," Sharon said.
paras.zh: 莎伦说：“这种纵向相关性表明，阿尔茨海默病的病理学与这一主要睡眠特征的破坏有关。”

paras.en: What Deep Sleep Reveals About the Aging Brain
paras.zh: 深度睡眠揭示了大脑老化的情况

paras.en: Although memory often declines with age, the new research indicates that the process may involve more than simply growing older. Changes associated with Alzheimer's disease, particularly tau accumulation in regions responsible for generating widespread slow waves, may help explain why some people experience greater difficulty retaining memories.
paras.zh: 尽管记忆力通常会随着年龄的增长而下降，但新的研究表明，这个过程可能不仅仅涉及年龄的增长。与阿尔茨海默病相关的变化，特别是负责产生广泛慢波的区域中 tau 蛋白的积累，可能有助于解释为什么有些人在保留记忆方面会遇到更大的困难。

paras.en: "It's not just about age," Sharon said. "It's how much pathology you have in frontal areas where global waves originate."
paras.zh: “这不仅仅是年龄的问题，”莎伦说。 “这取决于全球波起源的额叶区域有多少病态。”

paras.en: Sleep quality also appears to be part of the picture. Although it can be difficult to define or measure precisely, the organization and movement of slow brain waves may provide important indicators of how effectively the brain performs its nighttime memory functions.
paras.zh: 睡眠质量似乎也是问题的一部分。尽管很难精确定义或测量，但慢脑电波的组织和运动可以提供大脑如何有效执行其夜间记忆功能的重要指标。

paras.en: The findings raise the possibility that changes in deep sleep activity could eventually help researchers better understand or identify early memory problems. They also point toward potential targets for future treatments aimed at protecting memory as people age.
paras.zh: 这些发现提出了一种可能性，即深度睡眠活动的变化最终可以帮助研究人员更好地理解或识别早期记忆问题。他们还指出了未来治疗的潜在目标，旨在随着人们年龄的增长保护记忆。

paras.en: For now, however, a central question remains unanswered. Scientists still need to determine whether accumulating tau contributes to the breakdown of synchronized sleep waves, whether changes in those waves influence tau accumulation, or whether the relationship involves additional processes.
paras.zh: 然而，目前一个核心问题仍未得到解答。科学家们仍然需要确定 tau 蛋白的积累是否会导致同步睡眠波的破坏，这些波的变化是否会影响 tau 蛋白的积累，或者这种关系是否涉及其他过程。

paras.en: "We can see tau and lonely waves rising together over time," Sharon said. "What we cannot yet say is which leads -- and that question will shape how we design interventions."
paras.zh: “我们可以看到 tau 蛋白波和孤独波随着时间的推移一起上升，”莎伦说。 “我们还不能确定哪个是主导——这个问题将决定我们如何设计干预措施。”

paras.en: The study's additional co-authors include Xi Chen, James Westphal, Chelsea Brown, and Vyoma D. Shah of UC Berkeley, along with Jason Dude of Washington University in St. Louis.
paras.zh: 该研究的其他合著者包括加州大学伯克利分校的 Xi Chen、James Westphal、Chelsea Brown 和 Vyoma D. Shah，以及圣路易斯华盛顿大学的 Jason Dude。

paras.en: Funding came from grants awarded by the National Institute on Aging at the National Institutes of Health. Sharon also received support through a Glenn Foundation for Medical Research Postdoctoral Fellowship and a Weill Neurohub Fellowship.
paras.zh: 资金来自美国国立卫生研究院国家老龄化研究所授予的赠款。沙龙还获得了格伦医学研究基金会博士后奖学金和威尔神经中心奖学金的支持。
