paras.en: Sanders: These voice clones have been transformative for people who have lost the ability to talk. But the existence of realistic digital copies of voices has effects that ripple farther out into society.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些声音克隆对于那些失去说话能力的人来说是变革性的。但真实的声音数字副本的存在会对社会产生更深远的影响。

paras.en: Hany Farid: So here’s where sort of state of the art is. Today, with nothing more than a keyboard and an internet connection, you can type and you can get an image, a voice, a video of anything, anybody doing or saying anything.
paras.zh: Hany Farid：这就是最先进的地方。如今，只需键盘和互联网连接，您就可以打字，并且可以获得任何内容、任何人所做或所说的任何图像、声音、视频。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Hany Farid. He’s a computer scientist at Dartmouth College and cofounder of Get Real Security, a firm that sorts real from fake. I called him to ask how these voice clones have changed our world.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是汉尼·法里德。他是达特茅斯学院的计算机科学家，也是 Get Real Security 的联合创始人，这是一家辨别真假的公司。我打电话给他，询问这些声音克隆如何改变了我们的世界。

paras.en: Farid: If you had asked me, I don’t know, five years ago, is this possible? I would say, yeah, maybe, but not anytime soon. And then all of a sudden, boom, it just came out of nowhere.
paras.zh: Farid：如果你五年前问我，我不知道这可能吗？我会说，是的，也许吧，但不会很快。然后突然之间，砰的一声，它就凭空出现了。

paras.en: Sanders: This shift happened in a very, very short amount of time, and it has big implications, both good and bad.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这种转变发生在非常非常短的时间内，它产生了巨大的影响，无论好坏。

paras.en: Farid: And so we are living in, I think, in equal parts an exciting time and a terrifying time, and somehow those are coexisting.
paras.zh: 法里德：所以我认为，我们生活在一个激动人心的时代和一个可怕的时代，而且不知何故，这些时代是共存的。

paras.en: Sanders: Farid tells me about some of his research, which asks people to decide whether something, like a voice or a video, is real.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德向我介绍了他的一些研究，该研究要求人们判断某些事物（例如声音或视频）是否真实。

paras.en: Farid: My bread and butter is developing technologies to distinguish real from fake. And we work with media outlets and law enforcement and courts, et cetera. But one of the questions you always want to ask when you’re in my business is, well, do you need the mathematics and the computation? Just let somebody listen to it or look at it. And can they tell the difference?
paras.zh: Farid：我的面包和黄油正在开发区分真假的技术。我们与媒体、执法部门和法院等合作。但是，当你从事我的业务时，你总是想问的问题之一是，你需要数学和计算吗？只要让某人听或看即可。他们能分辨出区别吗？

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out they cannot. In laboratory tests, people can’t reliably say whether a voice they hear was created by a machine or by a real living, breathing person.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明他们不能。在实验室测试中，人们无法可靠地判断他们听到的声音是由机器发出的还是由真实存在的、会呼吸的人发出的。

paras.en: Farid: It’s essentially like they’re flipping a coin.
paras.zh: Farid：这本质上就像他们在掷硬币。

paras.en: Sanders: But there’s another, even higher bar for voice clones to pass. That’s whether they can mimic a specific person well enough to slip by undetected.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是声音克隆还有另一个甚至更高的门槛。问题在于它们是否能够很好地模仿特定的人，从而在不被发现的情况下溜走。

paras.en: Farid: The other question too is what if I, for example, play a real voice sample of your voice, Laura, and then I clone your voice using my favorite AI cloning technology, and then I type something and I get you to say something, and I play those two samples to somebody, and I don’t ask them if it’s real/fake. I say, is this the same person? Is the AI not only able to make something that is natural, but is it identity preserving?
paras.zh: Farid：另一个问题是，如果我播放你声音的真实声音样本，劳拉，然后我使用我最喜欢的人工智能克隆技术克隆你的声音，然后我输入一些东西，让你说一些东西，然后我向某人播放这两个样本，我不会问他们是真是假。我说，这是同一个人吗？人工智能不仅能够制造出自然的东西，而且还能保留身份吗？

paras.en: Sanders: Okay, give it a try yourself. Is this the same person?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：好吧，你自己尝试一下。这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: [Sanders voice clone] And how about now? Is this the same person?
paras.zh: [桑德斯的声音克隆]现在怎么样？这是同一个人吗？

paras.en: Farid: And when you ask them, is it the same person? They say yes, which means the AI has figured out with roughly 20 seconds or so of your voice how to make their AI sound like you, which is mind-blowing.
paras.zh: Farid：当你问他们时，是同一个人吗？他们说是，这意味着人工智能已经通过你大约 20 秒左右的声音弄清楚了如何让他们的人工智能听起来像你，这令人兴奋。

paras.en: Sanders: In the earlier episodes of this season, you’ve heard examples of the good that’s been created by these technological leaps. In many cases, that good comes because these voices are both extremely realistic and extremely good at sounding like a specific person. People want their voice to sound like theirs.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在本季的前几集中，你已经听说过这些技术飞跃所创造的美好例子。在许多情况下，这种好处的出现是因为这些声音非常真实，而且非常擅长听起来像特定的人。人们希望自己的声音听起来像自己的。

paras.en: Farid: People with ALS can speak with what sounds like their voice. We’ve seen beautiful examples of that. Translation, right? We can now translate things in real time from any language and it’ll sound like you. I’ve made videos of myself speaking any language I want and it sounds like me, and it’s amazing. It’s really cool.
paras.zh: Farid：患有 ALS 的人可以用听起来像他们自己的声音说话。我们已经看到了这方面的美丽例子。翻译一下吧？我们现在可以实时翻译任何语言的内容，而且听起来就像您一样。我制作了自己说任何我想要的语言的视频，听起来就像我一样，这太棒了。真的很酷。

paras.en: Sanders: These new ways to connect are very impressive, but as with any technology, these powerful realistic auditory dupes can be repurposed to cause harm.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些新的连接方式非常令人印象深刻，但与任何技术一样，这些强大的现实听觉欺骗可以被重新利用以造成伤害。

paras.en: Farid: Some pretty bad stuff’s happening, right? So let’s just go through a few of these. So first, you’re seeing massive types of fraud. Everything from romance scams to people calling parents and saying your kids have been taken, pay a ransom, to geopolitics. People are getting on calls with who they think are leaders of other countries, and it’s not. It’s a deepfake. It’s an AI-generated voice or face.
paras.zh: Farid：一些非常糟糕的事情正在发生，对吧？让我们来看看其中的一些。首先，您会看到大量类型的欺诈行为。从爱情骗局到人们打电话给父母并说你的孩子被带走了，需要支付赎金，再到地缘政治。人们正在与他们认为是其他国家领导人的人通话，但事实并非如此。这是一个深度伪造。这是人工智能生成的声音或面孔。

paras.en: Sanders: What Farid is saying feels especially relevant right now. I’m recording this episode in the fall of 2026, and midterm elections in the U.S. are upon us. Political ads are everywhere. Some of these ads use deepfake audio and video to make opponents say or do things they never did. Here are a few recent examples of deepfakes compiled by the New York Times.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：法里德所说的话现在感觉特别有意义。我在 2026 年秋天录制这一集，美国中期选举即将到来。政治广告无处不在。其中一些广告使用深度伪造的音频和视频来让对手说或做他们从未做过的事情。以下是《纽约时报》最近整理的一些深度伪造的例子。

paras.en: [Audio] Hi, I’m Zohran Mamdani and I’m Kathy Hochul and together, we’re making New York, don’t say affordable. I’m voting for Hochul because she basically gave me an early retirement. They stopped prosecuting people for crime, so now I get to sit back and play Candy Crush all day. Is New York getting a little expensive? I’m Kathy Hochul, and I’ve got just the thing. Clinton lover, Trump hater.
paras.zh: [音频] 大家好，我是 Zohran Mamdani，我是 Kathy Hochul，我们一起打造纽约，更不用说负担得起了。我投票给 Hochul，因为她基本上让我提前退休。他们不再起诉犯罪分子，所以现在我可以坐下来玩一整天的《糖果粉碎传奇》。纽约是不是有点贵了？我是凯西·霍赫尔（Kathy Hochul），我就是这样。克林顿的爱人，特朗普的仇恨者。

paras.en: Farid: When you can steal somebody’s likeness, their voice, and their face, you can do some damage. We’re seeing people doing content credential resets at companies. They call up and say, oh, I’m employee X. Will you reset my credential? That’s how they’re now attacking companies. We’re seeing North Korean IT workers penetrating Fortune 500 companies by disguising their voices and their accents and their identities. So lots of bad things, and not unpredictably bad.
paras.zh: 法里德：当你可以窃取某人的肖像、声音和面孔时，你就可以造成一些损害。我们看到人们在公司进行内容凭证重置。他们打电话说，哦，我是员工 X。您能重置我的凭据吗？这就是他们现在攻击公司的方式。我们看到朝鲜 IT 员工通过掩饰声音、口音和身份渗透到财富 500 强公司。所以有很多坏事，但并不是不可预测的坏事。

paras.en: Sanders: There are romance scams, political scams, employment scams, money scams of all sorts. Farid was even involved in one himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有爱情骗局、政治骗局、就业骗局、金钱骗局等等。法里德本人甚至也参与其中。

paras.en: Farid: My voice was cloned by an attacker. I was working a very sensitive case with an attorney. Not many people knew about it. And he got a call from my phone number in my voice talking about the case. And after about three minutes, got suspicious, hung up, called me back. Wasn’t me.
paras.zh: Farid：我的声音被攻击者克隆了。我正在和一位律师一起处理一个非常敏感的案件。没有多少人知道这件事。他接到了我的电话号码的电话，我的声音谈论着这个案子。大约三分钟后，我开始怀疑，挂断电话，给我回了电话。不是我。

paras.en: Sanders: With the proliferation of AI chatbots to write the scripts for these fake voices, these scams can be deployed on a very large scale. That means there’s no human in the loop except for the person getting scammed. There’s something depressing about the loss of this extremely personal information. And the worst part is that these cloned voices feel like they’re just the latest piece of privacy eroding.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：随着人工智能聊天机器人为这些虚假声音编写脚本的激增，这些骗局可以大规模部署。这意味着除了被骗的人之外，没有人参与其中。丢失这些极其个人的信息令人沮丧。最糟糕的是，这些克隆声音让人感觉它们只是最新的隐私侵蚀行为。

paras.en: Farid: For a long time, it was our social security numbers, our ability to access our bank accounts were held very tight. And then it’s like, all right, that’s over. Everybody’s got my social security. All the privacy problems of the last 20 years. So we’ve given up what we call PII, personally identifiable information. You can find my phone number, my address, my social security number, everything about me. And that’s true of almost every single American and every person in the world. All right, so that barrier was shattered, whatever, a few years ago. But then we held on to, okay, but I’ve got me, my voice, my likeness. Yeah, not so much. So now imagine that you have all the information you need about you, Laura, me, anybody, and now you can mimic me. Think about how powerful that is. And think about also how helpless I am. I have no control on the billions of calls unfolding every day, every hour, if somebody has co-opted my likeness.
paras.zh: 法里德：很长一段时间以来，我们的社会安全号码、我们访问银行账户的能力都受到严格控制。然后就好像，好吧，就这样结束了。每个人都有我的社会保障。过去 20 年的所有隐私问题。因此，我们放弃了所谓的 PII，即个人身份信息。你可以找到我的电话号码、我的地址、我的社会安全号码，以及关于我的一切。几乎每个美国人和世界上每个人都是如此。好吧，无论如何，几年前这个障碍就被打破了。但后来我们坚持了下来，好吧，但我有我自己，我的声音，我的肖像。是的，没那么多。现在想象一下，你拥有关于你、劳拉、我、任何人的所有信息，现在你可以模仿我。想想那有多么强大。也想想我是多么的无助。如果有人盗用了我的肖像，我无法控制每天、每小时发生的数十亿个电话。

paras.en: Sanders: Bigger picture, we’ve reached a point where it’s safe to say we can no longer automatically trust digital versions of other people. That applies to the images and sounds on my computer screen as I talked with Farid. Maybe this 2-D picture and sound coming from my laptop is a fake.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从更大的角度来看，我们已经到了可以肯定地说我们不能再自动信任其他人的数字版本的地步。这适用于我与法里德交谈时电脑屏幕上的图像和声音。也许我笔记本电脑上发出的二维图像和声音是假的。

paras.en: Farid: So this two-dimensional version that you and I are sharing now, all right, I can’t control that. That can be stolen. The three-dimensional is right now still me, right? We don’t have the robots that can mimic us. Yet is the end of that sentence.
paras.zh: Farid：所以你和我现在分享的这个二维版本，好吧，我无法控制。那可以被盗。现在的三维还是我吧？我们没有可以模仿我们的机器人。然而这句话已经结束了。

paras.en: Sanders: So my interview with Farid was alarming. There are parallels here to any new technology, though. Today, people talk about brain rot from junk online. But remember that television was also going to rot our brains.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以我对法里德的采访令人震惊。不过，这与任何新技术都有相似之处。如今，人们谈论网络垃圾导致的大脑腐烂。但请记住，电视也会腐蚀我们的大脑。

paras.en: [Audio] Its content affects us. So does the sheer weight of the hours we watch.
paras.zh: [音频]它的内容影响着我们。我们观看的时间的绝对重量也是如此。

paras.en: Sanders: Phones today are the downfall of society, but actual wired telephones encountered really similar resistance when they first started appearing in homes.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：今天的电话是社会的衰落，但真正的有线电话在刚开始出现在家庭中时也遇到了类似的阻力。

paras.en: [Audio] In Chicago, Sharon Krall’s 15-year-old daughter Angie got so addicted to one teen talk line, she ran up an $850 bill in one month.
paras.zh: [音频] 在芝加哥，莎朗·克拉尔 (Sharon Krall) 15 岁的女儿安吉 (Angie) 沉迷于青少年谈话台词，一个月内就花光了 850 美元的账单。

paras.en: Sanders: No big technological advance has escaped this fear.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：任何重大的技术进步都无法逃脱这种恐惧。

paras.en: [Audio] We need teachers who are deeply concerned about how the modern media of communication are changing education.
paras.zh: [音频]我们需要深切关注现代传播媒体如何改变教育的教师。

paras.en: Sanders: Electricity, bicycles, railways, novels, even the printing press all had their skeptics. So this fear of the new thing has been around a long time. Are synthetic voices created by AI any different? Here’s Karina Nagin from Bridging Voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：电力、自行车、铁路、小说，甚至印刷机都有怀疑论者。所以这种对新事物的恐惧已经存在很长时间了。人工智能创建的合成声音有什么不同吗？这是来自 Bridging Voice 的卡琳娜·纳金 (Karina Nagin) 的报道。

paras.en: Nagin: Taking off my Bridging Voice hat and just as like a human being in the world, I think there’s a lot of things about AI that I’m very concerned. Deepfakes, the ability to make videos and audio that sound and look just like someone saying something that they’re not saying, I think is a huge, huge concern to our news and public information.
paras.zh: Nagin：摘下我的桥接语音帽子，就像世界上的人类一样，我认为人工智能有很多我非常关心的事情。 Deepfakes，即制作视频和音频听起来和看起来就像有人在说他们没有说的话的能力，我认为这是我们新闻和公共信息的一个巨大的担忧。

paras.en: Sanders: Nagin then pivots back to the good, the possibilities here.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：纳金然后回到好的方面，这里的可能性。

paras.en: Nagin: And then I put on my little hat in my space that I am like, this is how we can harness this to impact people’s lives in our space right now. And I think both conversations need to happen.
paras.zh: 纳金：然后我在我的空间里戴上我的小帽子，我想，这就是我们如何利用它来影响我们空间中人们的生活。我认为这两种对话都需要进行。

paras.en: Sanders: It occurs to me that I’m seeing the ends of the spectrum here. The stories Farid told me were awful. And the stories that Jules and Casey and others have told me were really, really life-changingly good. Yet these ends of the spectrum are the easy ones. The ones you can look at and say, that’s a horrible way to use this technology. Or that is a powerful and good way to use a voice clone. Between those two poles is the middle ground. That’s the place where Snoop explains cell biology.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我觉得我看到了这个范围的两端。法里德给我讲的故事很糟糕。朱尔斯、凯西和其他人告诉我的故事真的非常非常好，足以改变我的生活。然而，这些极端都是容易的。你可以看到并说，这是使用这项技术的可怕方式。或者说，这是使用语音克隆的一种强大且良好的方法。这两极之间是中间地带。这就是 Snoop 解释细胞生物学的地方。

paras.en: [Audio] The membrane separates the material outside the cell.
paras.zh: [音频] 膜将细胞外的物质分开。

paras.en: Sanders: Good, because it’s helping people learn more about mitochondria and who couldn’t use more of that in their lives. Bad, because Snoop never actually said those words, and it’s weird to pretend otherwise.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它可以帮助人们更多地了解线粒体，以及那些在生活中无法使用更多线粒体的人。糟糕的是，因为史努比实际上从未说过这些话，而且假装不这么说很奇怪。

paras.en: [Audio] The artists of the Renaissance said that man’s main concern should be for man.
paras.zh: [音频]文艺复兴时期的艺术家说，人的主要关心应该是为了人。

paras.en: Sanders: There are deepfakes of the late great physicist Richard Feynman delivering famous lectures.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：已故伟大物理学家理查德·费曼发表著名演讲的深度伪造品。

paras.en: [Audio] The problem is the laws of physics themselves. Let me start with something basic. The next star over from us is called Proxima Centauri.
paras.zh: [音频] 问题在于物理定律本身。让我从一些基本的事情开始。我们附近的下一颗恒星叫做比邻星。

paras.en: Sanders: Good because it introduces some amazing physics to people who would otherwise scroll past? Bad because it’s somewhat disrespectful and possibly inaccurate? There aren’t easy answers here. This murky middle gets even murkier with the invention of griefbots. Those are digital versions of people who have passed away. And that means that special voices can keep talking to us long after the body that created them is gone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：很好，因为它向那些原本会滚动过去的人介绍了一些令人惊奇的物理学？不好是因为它有点不尊重而且可能不准确？这里没有简单的答案。随着悲伤机器人的发明，这个阴暗的中间变得更加阴暗。这些是已故之人的数字版本。这意味着特殊的声音可以在创造它们的身体消失很久之后继续与我们交谈。

paras.en: I read a poignant post online written by a guy who had lost his dad after years of dementia. He missed his dad’s voice, he wrote, so he cloned it. He paid for the starter pack, submitted three minutes of his dad’s audio, and he wrote, quote, a few minutes later, I had a scarily accurate clone of my dead father’s voice. He goes on to write, quote, my family and I had a good cathartic cry upon hearing the results. I had his cloned voice read the Lord’s Prayer as well as ‘Twas the Night before Christmas. Just hearing his simulated voice again is such a blessing and is helping me in the grief process. End quote.
paras.zh: 我在网上读到一篇令人心酸的帖子，作者是一位因多年痴呆症而失去父亲的人。他写道，他想念父亲的声音，所以他克隆了它。他支付了入门包的费用，提交了三分钟的他父亲的音频，然后他写道，几分钟后，我就得到了我已故父亲的声音的极其准确的克隆。他继续写道，引用，我和我的家人在听到结果后哭了一场。我让他的克隆声音朗读了主祷文以及《这是圣诞节前夜》。再次听到他的模拟声音真是一件幸事，并且正在帮助我度过悲伤的过程。结束报价。

paras.en: There are lots of companies now offering this exact thing. A casual search online gets me to a company that sells chats with dead loved ones. There’s a big orange button to click that says bring them back to life. A 2024 documentary called “Eternal You” follows the stories of people as they grapple with this idea. Here’s a little bit of the trailer.
paras.zh: 现在有很多公司提供这种产品。在网上随意搜索，我找到了一家销售与已故亲人聊天的公司。有一个橙色的大按钮可以点击，上面写着让它们复活。一部 2024 年的纪录片《永恒的你》讲述了人们与这个想法作斗争的故事。这是预告片的一小部分。

paras.en: [Audio] We are on the verge of a new era. Hi. It’s like, it’s the funniest thing. It’s like, what’s the first thing you say to someone that’s dead? Like, welcome back.
paras.zh: [音频]我们正处于新时代的边缘。你好。就像，这是最有趣的事情。就像，你对死去的人说的第一句话是什么？就像，欢迎回来。

paras.en: Sanders: Griefbots or digital avatars of loved ones offer a bridge from the past to the present, a way to remember vividly. But they are also a denial, of sorts, that all life must come to an end.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：悲伤机器人或亲人的数字化身提供了从过去到现在的桥梁，是一种生动地记住的方式。但它们也在某种程度上否认所有生命都必须结束。

paras.en: [Audio] And what I can tell you is that AI really is changing the way that we interact with death.
paras.zh: [音频]我可以告诉你的是，人工智能确实正在改变我们与死亡互动的​​方式。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s from a 2025 TEDx talk from Dylan Thomas Doyle. He’s a former hospital chaplain, current academic researcher at Northwestern University and self-described philosophy bro. His work explores death and AI.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是迪伦·托马斯·道尔 (Dylan Thomas Doyle) 2025 年 TEDx 演讲中的内容。他曾是一名医院牧师，现任西北大学学术研究员，自称是哲学兄弟。他的作品探索死亡和人工智能。

paras.en: [Audio] Imagine that you are at a funeral, and you’re sitting there in silent reflection, and all of a sudden, on the back screen in the auditorium, a woman’s face appears. And it’s the face of a woman named Marina. And her hologram, she starts talking to you, and she starts asking you how you’re doing today. And you answer her, and then you ask her a question back. And she responds as if she is still there.
paras.zh: [音频]想象一下，你正在参加一场葬礼，你坐在那里默默地沉思，突然，礼堂的后屏幕上出现了一张女人的脸。这是一个名叫玛丽娜的女人的脸。和她的全息图，她开始和你说话，她开始问你今天过得怎么样。你回答她，然后你反问她一个问题。她的反应就好像她还在那里一样。

paras.en: Sanders: I called Doyle to ask about the implications of using technology this way.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我打电话给多伊尔询问以这种方式使用技术的影响。

paras.en: Doyle: It was on my radar as a chaplain and a technology researcher, I started thinking through, well, what is the actual impact of this technology on people? So what is it like to hear the voice, in the context of this podcast, the voice of, say, your father who’s passed away while you’re actively grieving their death? And they’re not just repeating what they said or a journal entry in their voice, but like, creating new stories and new relationships through their voice. It gives a lot of people existential ick, is what I’ve heard. And that’s something that I really, I’m curious about.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：作为一名牧师和技术研究员，我开始思考这项技术对人们的实际影响是什么？那么，在这个播客的背景下，听到你的父亲的声音，比如说，当你正在积极哀悼他们的死亡时，听到他去世的声音是什么感觉？他们不仅仅是用自己的声音重复自己所说的话或日记条目，而是通过自己的声音创造新的故事和新的关系。据我所知，它让很多人感到厌恶。这确实是我很好奇的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: There’s tension here, Doyle tells me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔告诉我，这里存在紧张局势。

paras.en: Doyle: So there’s this push force where you’re like, this is not right. We don’t have the narrative or cultural script to understand what’s going on there. But then as people are beginning to use it, there’s a comfort that comes out of it. So we’re working in that tension space between this comfort that comes, then you’re still dealing with this push away from this technology of it just being weird in a way that people are still grappling with language, I think, to describe.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：所以你会觉得有一种推力，这是不对的。我们没有叙事或文化脚本来理解那里正在发生的事情。但当人们开始使用它时，就会产生一种安慰。因此，我们正在这种即将到来的舒适感之间的紧张空间中工作，然后你仍然在处理这种远离这项技术的情况，它只是以一种奇怪的方式，我认为，人们仍在努力用语言来描述。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s not clear how these types of interactions might affect grieving. They could help or they could hurt.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：目前尚不清楚这些类型的互动如何影响悲伤。他们可能会提供帮助，也可能会造成伤害。

paras.en: Doyle: There is this tension between more healthy continuing bonds. So continuing that relationship by, say, writing letters to your dead loved one or, you know, talking out loud to them and continuing that relationship in a positive way that moves us through a healthy grief process and a grief journey. Or hanging on to our relationship with that person to a degree where we can’t actually do any sort of moving on.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：更健康的持续关系之间存在着这种紧张关系。因此，通过给已故亲人写信，或者大声地与他们交谈，以积极的方式继续这种关系，让我们度过一个健康的悲伤过程和悲伤之旅，来继续这种关系。或者我们紧紧抓住与那个人的关系，以至于我们实际上无法采取任何行动。

paras.en: Sanders: Doyle points out that we don’t have good data on how many people might be using griefbots.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：多伊尔指出，我们没有关于有多少人可能使用悲伤机器人的良好数据。

paras.en: Doyle: I just don’t want us to get ahead of ourselves when it comes to people like using these. So the capability to do everything we’ve talked about with griefbots is there. But the actual use cases of individuals in their homes using this, it’s still pretty unclear about the adoption of those technologies.
paras.zh: 多伊尔：我只是不想让我们在谈到喜欢使用这些的人时表现得超前。因此，悲伤机器人有能力完成我们谈到的所有事情。但个人在家中使用该技术的实际用例，这些技术的采用情况仍然相当不清楚。

paras.en: Sanders: But even if griefbots aren’t widespread, the questions they raise aren’t going away. These voices are blurring the lines between a memory and a present-day experience, between alive and dead. Here’s Karina Nagin again.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但即使悲伤机器人并不普遍，它们提出的问题也不会消失。这些声音模糊了记忆与当下经历、生与死之间的界限。卡琳娜·纳金又来了。

paras.en: Nagin: It’s an interesting conversation that we’re having right now of what happens to your voice once you pass away. Some people are starting to integrate this into their wills or their sort of final wishes of, do you want your voice to be able to speak at your own memorial service?
paras.zh: 纳金：我们现在正在进行一场有趣的对话，内容是关于你去世后你的声音会发生什么。有些人开始将其融入他们的遗嘱或最终愿望中，你希望你的声音能够在你自己的追悼会上发言吗？

paras.en: Do you want to have messages saved in your voice that are for your child at graduation that they listen to? Who and when can use that? I think that these are things that people are starting to think about. Who owns your voice? Can your children use your voice to write a speech for their children’s graduation? Or do you want that voice to be deleted once you pass away? Very tricky questions.
paras.zh: 您是否想在您的声音中保存留言供您的孩子在毕业典礼上聆听？谁以及何时可以使用它？我认为这些是人们开始思考的事情。谁拥有你的声音？您的孩子可以用您的声音为孩子的毕业典礼写演讲稿吗？或者你希望在你去世后删除那个声音？非常棘手的问题。

paras.en: Sanders: Rules about who can use voice clones are all over the place. Regulations vary by state and by country, and even companies have their own individual policies in place. There are no clear guidelines, and that makes sense given how young this technology is. Conversations about digital voices and how to use them are inherently very personal. There are as many different takes as there are people. I asked MA if she and Jules had talked about this.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：关于谁可以使用语音克隆的规则无处不在。法规因州和国家而异，甚至公司也有自己的个人政策。目前还没有明确的指导方针，考虑到这项技术还很年轻，这是有道理的。关于数字语音以及如何使用它们的对话本质上是非常个人化的。有多少人，就有多少种不同的看法。我问妈妈她和朱尔斯是否谈过这件事。

paras.en: MA: I love that question. Both of us love this question because it’s so important. And we talked about it before he got the trache. Like when he was already using the voice, we were talking about different things in bed at night. And he said, you know, I have a very clear request that my voice like dies with me, basically, that, you know, I ask that you don’t use the voice to keep me alive in any way, that there’s no… And I was like, 100 percent clear. I hadn’t even thought about that. But yeah, it would make sense to be like, I miss him so much. I want to, whatever or. But no, as far as we’re concerned, his voice dies when he does. And his voice will live on in whatever videos or things we captured, whatever he’s left us intentionally. And that’s as far as that goes.
paras.zh: MA：我喜欢这个问题。我们俩都喜欢这个问题，因为它非常重要。在他接受气管切开术之前我们就讨论过这件事。就像当他已经使用这个声音时，我们晚上在床上谈论不同的事情。他说，你知道，我有一个非常明确的要求，我的声音会随着我一起消失，基本上，你知道，我要求你不要以任何方式使用声音让我活下去，没有……我的感觉是百分百清楚。我什至没有想到这一点。但是，是的，我非常想念他，这是有道理的。我想要，无论如何。但不，就我们而言，当他这样做时，他的声音就消失了。他的声音将永远存在于我们拍摄的任何视频或事物中，无论他故意留给我们什么。就这样了。

paras.en: Sanders: So when Jules is gone, his voice will be gone too. But right now is a different story.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以当朱尔斯去世时，他的声音也会消失。但现在情况不同了。

paras.en: MA: Well back in 2021, I was writing an Instagram post about something. It was him playing with Skylar in the backyard while he was already like, you know, had trouble with everything, but he was doing what he could. And I asked him like, you know, what, what do you want to caption it? And he just said that, right here, right now phrase, something else, and like right here, right now. And it became our family mantra. It became something that we wanted to just to share and in both a sense of like do the things that you want to do.
paras.zh: MA：早在 2021 年，我就在 Instagram 上写了一篇关于某件事的帖子。那是他和斯凯拉在后院玩耍，而他已经好像，你知道，一切都遇到了麻烦，但他正在尽力而为。我问他，你知道，你想给它加上什么标题吗？他只是说，就在这里，现在，短语，其他的东西，就像就在这里，现在。这成了我们家庭的座右铭。它成为我们想要分享的东西，从某种意义上说，就像做你想做的事情。

paras.en: And also something that’s always been big for Jules that I’ve admired him articulate is that it’s not just about, oh, just go forward and do all the things and like suck the marrow out of life. It’s like just also, like, settle. Like it doesn’t have to be that extreme, you know. There’s a beautiful thing about that presence and that settling in. And again, with ALS being something where you’re given the diagnosis, which is terminal, it’s basically a death sentence. Most people are given, you know, two to five years. You don’t know where you’re going to fall in that. We’ve known people that have passed away in a year and a half. We’ve known people that are six years in like Jules, but can still kind of walk around, speak a little bit. ALS touches everybody really differently. So you really don’t know what’s coming. And there’s a lot of like forward thinking that you can do that detaches you from being in your life. So how are you here? And then there’s a lot of backwards, you know, reminiscing and grieving about all the things we’ve lost and how we wish things were different. But then that also takes you out of like this moment right now and this part of your story.
paras.zh: 对朱尔斯来说，我很钦佩他能表达出来的一直很重要的一点是，这不仅仅是，哦，继续前进，做所有的事情，就像从生活中吸取骨髓一样。这就像也，就像，安顿下来。你知道，事情不必那么极端。这种存在和安定下来是一件美好的事情。再说一次，当你被诊断出 ALS 时，这是晚期的，基本上就等于被判了死刑。你知道，大多数人都会被给予两到五年的时间。你不知道自己会陷入其中。我们认识一年半内去世的人。我们认识像朱尔斯这样六岁的人，但仍然可以四处走动，说一点话。 ALS 对每个人的影响确实不同。所以你真的不知道会发生什么。你可以做很多类似的前瞻性思考，让你脱离生活。那么你在这里怎么样？然后有很多倒退，你知道，回忆和悲伤我们失去的所有东西，以及我们如何希望事情有所不同。但这也会让你脱离现在的这一刻和故事的这一部分。

paras.en: Sanders: This part of the story is the important part. Right here, right now.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：故事的这一部分是重要的部分。就在这里，就是现在。

paras.en: On the next and final episode of The Deep End, Talk to Me. We’re going to look at what’s next for Jules and Casey and what’s next for the science racing to give voices back to people.
paras.zh: 在《深渊》的下一集也是最后一集中，《跟我说话》。我们将看看朱尔斯和凯西的下一步是什么，以及科学竞赛的下一步是什么，以回馈人们的声音。

paras.en: Vikash Gilja: We can see all the pieces coming together. All of the emphasis, capital, quite frankly, talent focused on advancing AI techniques and technologies. You know, our little corner can benefit from it, right? These tools weren’t available even five years ago.
paras.zh: Vikash Gilja：我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。所有的重点、资本、坦率地说、人才都集中在推进人工智能技术和技术上。你知道，我们的小角落可以从中受益，对吗？这些工具在五年前还没有出现。

paras.en: Sanders: What’s next for the human voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：人声的下一步是什么？

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: Sanders: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：深渊是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: Sound credits: city park with bicycles and crows in springtime by Garuda1982, printing press spinning wheel.flac by kyles, Turning Pages 01.wav by AudioSea.
paras.zh: 声音来源：Garuda1982 的《春天有自行车和乌鸦的城市公园》、kyles 的印刷机纺轮.flac、AudioSea 的 Turning Pages 01.wav。

paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Record-low temperature created on China’s space station
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: Science has reached a new low. Temperature, that is.
paras.zh: 科学已经达到了新的低点。温度，就是。

paras.en: Scientists cooled a collection of atoms to about 10 picokelvins, or 10 trillionths of a kelvin. That’s barely a smidge above absolute zero (−273.15° Celsius). The atoms formed a Bose-Einstein condensate, a quantum state of matter, colder than any before, researchers report November 5 in Science.
paras.zh: 科学家将一组原子冷却至约 10 皮开尔文，即万亿分之一开尔文。这仅比绝对零（-273.15°摄氏度）高一点点。研究人员于 11 月 5 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，这些原子形成了玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，这是一种物质的量子态，其温度比以前任何时候都要低。

paras.en: To achieve that record-low chill, scientists took their work to space. The atoms orbited Earth aboard China’s Tiangong space station. There, researchers used laser-based traps to contain 20,000 rubidium atoms and reduce their motion, thereby cooling them. At an atomic level, temperature is tied to motion: Atoms and molecules in the air around us move more slowly when it’s colder. Similarly, in systems of cold atoms, scientists can define an effective temperature based on how slowly the atoms spread apart when they are allowed to expand.
paras.zh: 为了实现创纪录的最低寒冷，科学家们将他们的工作带到了太空。这些原子乘坐中国天宫空间站绕地球运行。在那里，研究人员使用基于激光的陷阱来容纳 20,000 个铷原子并减少它们的运动，从而冷却它们。在原子层面上，温度与运动有关：当温度较低时，我们周围空气中的原子和分子运动得更慢。同样，在冷原子系统中，科学家可以根据原子膨胀时扩散的速度来定义有效温度。

paras.en: On Earth, gravitational forces cause clouds of atoms to sag, reducing the effectiveness of cooling. But on the space station, the atoms experienced microgravity, the apparent weightlessness of an object in free fall.
paras.zh: 在地球上，重力会导致原子云下垂，从而降低冷却效率。但在空间站上，原子经历了微重力，即自由落体物体表面上的失重状态。

paras.en: To make a Bose-Einstein condensate, a disorderly gaggle of atoms is cooled until the atoms all take on the same quantum state, acting as one entity. By experimenting with ultracold atoms, researchers can study exotic states of matter and other mysterious physics. And they can test fundamental concepts, such as the equivalence principle — the idea that explains why objects of different masses fall at the same rate in a vacuum.
paras.zh: 为了制造玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，一群无序的原子被冷却，直到所有原子都呈现相同的量子态，充当一个实体。通过对超冷原子进行实验，研究人员可以研究奇异的物质状态和其他神秘的物理现象。他们还可以测试基本概念，例如等效原理——该原理解释了为什么不同质量的物体在真空中以相同的速度下落。

paras.en: Spacefaring Bose-Einstein condensates were previously made on the International Space Station, at effective temperatures as low as 52 picokelvins. And an experiment on Earth, in which atoms were dropped down a tower to induce weightlessness, reached 38 picokelvins. But drop tower experiments are limited by the time their free fall lasts. That’s not an issue for experiments in Earth’s orbit. So cold atoms in space are really taking off.
paras.zh: 太空玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体之前是在国际空间站上制造的，有效温度低至 52 皮开尔文。在地球上进行的一项实验中，原子从塔上落下以产生失重状态，温度达到了 38 皮开尔文。但落塔实验受到自由落体持续时间的限制。对于地球轨道上的实验来说，这不是问题。所以太空中的冷原子确实正在起飞。

articles.title: Scientists Discover an Unexpected Aging 'Cliff' in Sperm RNA
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: It takes two to tango, and yet when it comes to research on human reproduction, female fertility has historically taken the lead.
paras.zh: 探戈需要两个人，但在人类生殖研究方面，女性生育能力历来处于领先地位。

paras.en: Now, emerging research is putting a new foot forward.
paras.zh: 现在，新兴研究正在迈出新的一步。

paras.en: Sperm from older fathers may show more signs of aging than we thought, and not just from DNA mutations.
paras.zh: 年长父亲的精子可能表现出比我们想象的更多的衰老迹象，而不仅仅是 DNA 突变造成的。

paras.en: A recent study, published in The EMBO Journal, has reported a clear "aging cliff" in mouse sperm that hasn't been detected before.
paras.zh: 最近发表在《EMBO 杂志》上的一项研究报告称，小鼠精子出现了明显的“衰老悬崖”，这是以前从未检测到的。

paras.en: It has to do with RNA, which helps translate the instructions stored in DNA into proteins.
paras.zh: 它与 RNA 有关，RNA 有助于将 DNA 中存储的指令翻译成蛋白质。

paras.en: In mice, the mixture of small RNA fragments carried by sperm transitions sharply in midlife.
paras.zh: 在小鼠中，精子携带的小 RNA 片段混合物在中年发生急剧转变。

paras.en: Specifically, the heads of older sperm seem to contain more long pieces of RNA molecules and fewer short pieces.
paras.zh: 具体来说，老年精子的头部似乎含有更多的长RNA分子片段和更少的短片段。

paras.en: The same pattern was then confirmed in human samples, using two separate groups of donors.
paras.zh: 然后使用两组不同的捐赠者在人类样本中证实了相同的模式。

paras.en: This does not establish whether humans experience the same abrupt aging cliff, but the parallels are worth investigating further.
paras.zh: 这并不能确定人类是否会经历同样的突然衰老悬崖，但其中的相似之处值得进一步研究。

paras.en: "It's like finding a molecular clock that ticks with age in both mice and humans, suggesting a fundamental, conserved molecular signature of sperm aging," says urology researcher Qi Chen from the University of Utah.
paras.zh: 犹他大学泌尿学研究员 Qi Chen 表示：“这就像在小鼠和人类身上发现了一个随着年龄增长而滴答作响的分子钟，暗示了精子衰老的基本、保守的分子特征。”

paras.en: "Maybe this progressive length shift accumulates quietly, until it triggers the 'cliff' change at mid-life."
paras.zh: “也许这种渐进的长度变化会悄悄积累，直到在中年触发‘悬崖’变化。”

paras.en: For decades, scientists have known that as sperm age, they tend to accumulate more DNA damage and genetic mutations.
paras.zh: 几十年来，科学家们已经知道，随着精子年龄的增长，它们往往会积累更多的 DNA 损伤和基因突变。

paras.en: This has long been used to explain why male fertility declines with age, and why harmful mutations may be passed on to offspring.
paras.zh: 长期以来，这一直被用来解释为什么男性生育能力随着年龄的增长而下降，以及为什么有害的突变可能会遗传给后代。

paras.en: But it's not just DNA that sperm delivers to an egg. It also delivers fragments of RNA, possibly picked up in the epididymis, the duct that carries sperm out of the testes, and these too may matter for fertilization and development.
paras.zh: 但精子传递给卵子的不仅仅是DNA。它还提供 RNA 片段，可能是在附睾（将精子带出睾丸的管道）中获取的，这些也可能对受精和发育很重要。

paras.en: These RNA fragments may regulate early embryonic development, and some evidence suggests they may even pass environmental traits on to the next generation.
paras.zh: 这些RNA片段可能调节早期胚胎发育，一些证据表明它们甚至可能将环境特征传递给下一代。

paras.en: In older mouse sperm, fragments of rRNA appear to be longer.
paras.zh: 在老年小鼠精子中，rRNA 片段似乎更长。

paras.en: What's more, when researchers introduced RNA fragments resembling those of older sperm into mouse embryonic stem cells, they observed changes in the activity of genes associated with metabolism and neurodegeneration.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，当研究人员将类似于老年精子的RNA片段引入小鼠胚胎干细胞时，他们观察到与新陈代谢和神经退行性变相关的基因活性的变化。

paras.en: This suggests that age-related changes in the RNA molecules that sperm hold could influence how genes are expressed during early development.
paras.zh: 这表明精子所含 RNA 分子与年龄相关的变化可能会影响早期发育过程中基因的表达方式。

paras.en: The findings have "unveiled a novel sperm aging landscape" in both mice and humans, the authors argue, "heralding a new era in reproductive health where a deeper understanding of the 'sperm RNA code' helps shape healthier generations."
paras.zh: 作者认为，这些发现在小鼠和人类中“揭示了一种新的精子衰老现象”，“预示着生殖健康的新时代，对‘精子 RNA 密码’的更深入了解有助于塑造更健康的一代。”

paras.en: Developmental neuroscientist Noriko Osumi from Japan's Tohoku University was not involved in the research, but in an accompanying piece for The EMBO Journal, she explains why sperm RNA is a "particularly compelling" target for male fertility research.
paras.zh: 日本东北大学的发育神经科学家 Noriko Osumi 没有参与这项研究，但在《EMBO 杂志》的一篇附带文章中，她解释了为什么精子 RNA 是男性生育力研究“特别引人注目”的目标。

paras.en: "Sperm deliver more than a haploid genome," she writes.
paras.zh: “精子传递的不仅仅是单倍体基因组，”她写道。

paras.en: They also deliver RNA fragments, and these are "not merely passive remnants but part of the information delivered at fertilization". For instance, they can carry epigenetic information that could feasibly influence offspring development.
paras.zh: 它们还传递 RNA 片段，这些“不仅仅是被动残留物，而且是受精时传递的信息的一部分”。例如，它们可以携带可能影响后代发育的表观遗传信息。

paras.en: Today, in many parts of the world, parents are having kids later in life, and yet scientists know remarkably little about how male sex organs age and how that impacts reproduction or the health of future offspring.
paras.zh: 如今，在世界许多地方，父母生育孩子的年龄越来越大，但科学家们对男性性器官如何衰老以及这如何影响生殖或未来后代的健康知之甚少。

paras.en: A large study from the World Health Organization (WHO) involving 8,500 couples in 25 countries found that male factors contributed fully or at least in part to 45 percent of infertility cases.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织 (WHO) 一项涉及 25 个国家 8,500 对夫妇的大型研究发现，男性因素完全或至少部分导致了 45% 的不孕不育病例。

paras.en: In 2024, an editorial on male infertility in the journal Nature Reviews Urology argued that "the burden of male infertility is often unrecognized and its causes are poorly understood."
paras.zh: 2024 年，《自然评论泌尿学》杂志上一篇关于男性不育的社论认为，“男性不育的负担常常未被认识到，其原因也知之甚少。”

paras.en: This means that "men can be sidelined during treatment and the burden of medically assisted reproductive techniques falls on the woman, even if she herself has no reproductive issues," the editorial explained.
paras.zh: 这意味着“男性在治疗期间可以被边缘化，医疗辅助生殖技术的负担落在女性身上，即使她自己没有生殖问题，”社论解释道。

paras.en: This new research seeks to better understand how sperm function may decline with age.
paras.zh: 这项新研究旨在更好地了解精子功能如何随着年龄的增长而下降。

paras.en: Chen and colleagues now want to figure out why these RNA changes are occurring, and what can be done about it.
paras.zh: Chen 和同事现在想要弄清楚为什么会发生这些 RNA 变化，以及可以采取什么措施。

paras.en: "If we can understand the enzymes driving this shift, they could become actionable targets for interventions to potentially improve sperm quality in aging males," Chen says.
paras.zh: “如果我们能够了解驱动这种转变的酶，它们可能成为干预措施的可行目标，从而有可能改善老年男性的精子质量，”陈说。

paras.en: The research has been published in The EMBO Journal.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《EMBO 杂志》上。

articles.title: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch May Be Changing The Color of The Ocean
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: There's a monster lurking in the middle of the North Pacific Ocean, neither kraken nor Cthulhu, but a growing behemoth of humanity's creation.
paras.zh: 北太平洋中部潜伏着一种怪物，它既不是海怪，也不是克苏鲁，而是人类创造的一个不断增长的庞然大物。

paras.en: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is a vast, drifting accumulation of plastic trash, sprawling across an area roughly twice the size of Texas.
paras.zh: 大太平洋垃圾带是一片巨大的、漂浮的塑料垃圾堆积物，其面积大约是德克萨斯州面积的两倍。

paras.en: It's carried and concentrated by ocean currents, but it is not, as the description might suggest, a single congealed agglomeration of garbage. It's so diffusely spread that it cannot be detected in satellite images from Earth orbit.
paras.zh: 它被洋流携带和集中，但它并不像描述所暗示的那样，是一个单一的凝结的垃圾团块。它的传播范围如此之广，以至于无法在地球轨道上的卫星图像中检测到。

paras.en: The concentration of microplastics in the garbage patch may have become high enough to change the color of the ocean in which they drift, according to a new study by ocean optics specialists Shea Cheatham, Daniel Koestner, and Børge Hamre of the University of Bergen in Norway.
paras.zh: 挪威卑尔根大学海洋光学专家 Shea Cheatham、Daniel Koestner 和 Børge Hamre 的一项新研究表明，垃圾带中微塑料的浓度可能已经足够高，足以改变它们所漂浮的海洋的颜色。

paras.en: "We were shocked, excited, and a little alarmed to see the same shift in ocean color on the map after we analyzed the first satellite dataset of the garbage patch," Cheatham told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “在我们分析了垃圾带的第一个卫星数据集后，我们看到地图上海洋颜色发生了同样的变化，我们感到震惊、兴奋，还有点惊慌，”Cheatham 告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: "Our first reaction was disbelief, which is what led us to check two other satellite datasets just to convince ourselves that it was even remotely possible that we could be seeing the same signature evident in our models."
paras.zh: “我们的第一反应是难以置信，这导致我们检查了另外两个卫星数据集，只是为了说服自己，我们甚至有可能在我们的模型中看到相同的明显特征。”

paras.en: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch lies within a giant circular system of currents in the North Pacific called a gyre, which has become a catchment area for plastic detritus. A 2018 survey estimated that it contained some 1.8 trillion pieces of plastic, weighing around 79,000 metric tons.
paras.zh: 大太平洋垃圾带位于北太平洋一个名为环流的巨大环形洋流系统内，该系统已成为塑料碎屑的集水区。 2018 年的一项调查估计，其中含有约 1.8 万亿件塑料，重约 79,000 吨。

paras.en: Much of that mass consists of discarded fishing equipment, with a later study tracing a substantial proportion of the larger debris to fishing industries in Japan, China, South Korea, Taiwan, and the United States.
paras.zh: 其中大部分是废弃的捕鱼设备，后来的一项研究将大部分较大的碎片追溯到日本、中国、韩国、台湾和美国的渔业。

paras.en: But by sheer number, tiny fragments of microplastic dominate, accounting for an estimated 94 percent of the pieces floating in the patch, although only 8 percent of its total mass.
paras.zh: 但从数量上看，微塑料的微小碎片占主导地位，估计占该区域漂浮碎片的 94%，尽管只占总质量的 8%。

paras.en: The work of Cheatham and her colleagues began not with the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, but with how similar microplastic fragments interact with light in a marine environment.
paras.zh: 奇塔姆和她的同事的工作并不是从太平洋垃圾带开始，而是从类似的微塑料碎片如何与海洋环境中的光相互作用开始。

paras.en: Specifically, it grew out of laboratory research examining how microplastics absorb and scatter light, comparing their optical properties with those of naturally occurring materials in seawater, including phytoplankton and minerals.
paras.zh: 具体来说，它源于实验室研究，检查微塑料如何吸收和散射光，并将其光学特性与海水中天然存在的材料（包括浮游植物和矿物质）的光学特性进行比较。

paras.en: "We observed some unique properties that suggest that microplastics scatter and absorb light differently enough to potentially produce unique optical signatures which may be detectable in some oceanic environments," Cheatham explained.
paras.zh: 奇塔姆解释说：“我们观察到一些独特的特性，表明微塑料对光的散射和吸收差异足以产生独特的光学特征，这些特征在某些海洋环境中可以被检测到。”

paras.en: The researchers then turned to models to see if these signatures might be detectable with current satellite capabilities. Their simulations suggested that the optical effect may occur at microplastic concentrations potentially already swirling around in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后转向模型，看看当前的卫星能力是否可以检测到这些特征。他们的模拟表明，光学效应可能发生在可能已经在大太平洋垃圾带中旋转的微塑料浓度处。

paras.en: "We decided to take a look at existing satellite records to see if there were any changes in the ocean's color consistent with the signature of microplastics shown in our simulations," Cheatham said.
paras.zh: 奇塔姆说：“我们决定查看现有的卫星记录，看看海洋颜色是否发生了与我们模拟中显示的微塑料特征一致的变化。”

paras.en: Across satellite observations spanning 2002 to 2022, the researchers identified a subtle but statistically significant brightening of the ocean in blue and green wavelengths near the Great Pacific Garbage Patch – a gradually growing cyan tint.
paras.zh: 通过 2002 年至 2022 年的卫星观测，研究人员发现太平洋垃圾带附近的海洋在蓝色和绿色波长中出现了微妙但具有统计学意义的增亮现象，即逐渐增长的青色色调。

paras.en: It was consistent with the optical signature that their simulations had predicted microplastics might produce.
paras.zh: 这与他们的模拟预测微塑料可能产生的光学特征一致。

paras.en: Now, seawater can be pretty mucky. All sorts of particulate and dissolved matter drift around in it, and there's a lot more in the gyre than just trash.
paras.zh: 现在，海水可能非常浑浊。各种颗粒物和溶解物在其中漂流，而且漩涡中还有很多东西，而不仅仅是垃圾。

paras.en: But scientists also have a pretty good handle on what different clouds of marine miscellany look like from space.
paras.zh: 但科学家们也很好地掌握了从太空看不同的海洋杂物云的样子。

paras.en: Phytoplankton, for example, absorb blue and red wavelengths, leaving the ocean looking greener. Dissolved organic matter absorbs more blue light, giving water a darker or browner appearance.
paras.zh: 例如，浮游植物吸收蓝色和红色波长，使海洋看起来更绿。溶解的有机物吸收更多的蓝光，使水呈现更深或更棕色的外观。

paras.en: "What's interesting about the optical signature of microplastics is that they generally do not absorb much light at all across the visible spectrum, and are strong scatterers," Cheatham said.
paras.zh: “微塑料光学特征的有趣之处在于，它们通常在可见光谱范围内根本不吸收太多光，并且是强散射体，”奇塔姆说。

paras.en: "So they brighten the ocean, and this brightening preferentially occurs simultaneously at blue and green wavelengths."
paras.zh: “因此它们使海洋变亮，并且这种变亮优先在蓝色和绿色波长处同时发生。”

paras.en: That combination of blue and green brightening is unusual. Changes in phytoplankton or dissolved organic matter can alter the ocean's color, but their different absorption properties make them unlikely to produce quite the same effect.
paras.zh: 蓝色和绿色增亮的组合很不寻常。浮游植物或溶解有机物的变化可以改变海洋的颜色，但它们不同的吸收特性使它们不太可能产生完全相同的效果。

paras.en: Other particles, such as mineral dust, can also scatter sunlight and brighten the ocean. However, these tend to be more abundant in coastal waters, and measurements from a nearby research station showed a stable pattern of dust deposition over the study period.
paras.zh: 其他颗粒，例如矿物尘埃，也可以散射阳光并照亮海洋。然而，这些粉尘在沿海水域往往更为丰富，附近研究站的测量结果显示，在研究期间，粉尘沉积模式稳定。

paras.en: This doesn't conclusively establish that microplastics are responsible. The researchers found that certain combinations of natural environmental changes could produce a similar signature, although these scenarios were relatively rare in their simulations.
paras.zh: 这并不能最终证明微塑料是罪魁祸首。研究人员发现，自然环境变化的某些组合可以产生类似的特征，尽管这些场景在他们的模拟中相对罕见。

paras.en: Nevertheless, the correspondence between the predicted signature, the satellite observations, and their location in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch makes microplastics a compelling possible explanation.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，预测的特征、卫星观测及其在太平洋垃圾带中的位置之间的对应关系使得微塑料成为一个令人信服的可能解释。

paras.en: If it looks like microplastics in the garbage patch, it would be silly not to investigate the possibility of it being microplastics in the garbage patch.
paras.zh: 如果它看起来像垃圾带中的微塑料，那么不调查它是垃圾带中的微塑料的可能性就太愚蠢了。

paras.en: Which is where the researchers are now. Occam's razor may point toward microplastics, but proper scientific caution requires confirmation – and that means testing the seawater in the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.
paras.zh: 这就是研究人员现在所在的地方。奥卡姆剃刀可能指向微塑料，但适当的科学谨慎需要确认——这意味着测试大太平洋垃圾带的海水。

paras.en: "To fully answer the question of whether microplastics themselves are the root cause of this ocean color shift, we will need to go to the garbage patch to make optical measurements of water samples and quantify the microplastics present," Cheatham said.
paras.zh: 奇塔姆说：“为了充分回答微塑料本身是否是海洋颜色变化的根本原因的问题，我们需要前往垃圾带对水样进行光学测量并量化存在的微塑料。”

paras.en: "We're hopeful that we can do this work in the future."
paras.zh: “我们希望将来能够完成这项工作。”

paras.en: If those results confirm the researchers' suspicions, we can add yet another tally mark to the list of ways plastic pollution is changing the world on a large scale.
paras.zh: 如果这些结果证实了研究人员的怀疑，我们就可以在塑料污染大规模改变世界的方式清单上再添加一个记号。

paras.en: But microplastics may also present the biggest challenge to cleaning up the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, despite accounting for only a small proportion of its mass.
paras.zh: 但微塑料也可能对清理太平洋垃圾带构成最大挑战，尽管只占其质量的一小部分。

paras.en: Cleanup efforts have been able to remove larger pieces of junk. There's no such solution for tiny fragments.
paras.zh: 清理工作已经能够清除较大的垃圾。对于微小碎片没有这样的解决方案。

paras.en: "Removing microplastics from the water column, particularly the smallest plastics we focus on in our study, is essentially impossible, and these plastics are the most likely to enter the base of the marine food web and end up on your plate," Cheatham said.
paras.zh: 奇塔姆说：“从水体中去除微塑料，特别是我们研究中关注的最小塑料，基本上是不可能的，而且这些塑料最有可能进入海洋食物网的底部并最终出现在你的盘子里。”

paras.en: "At present, the only way to reduce microplastic pollution is to prevent them from entering the water in the first place."
paras.zh: “目前，减少微塑料污染的唯一方法是首先阻止它们进入水中。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Communications Earth & Environment.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《通讯地球与环境》杂志上。

articles.title: 2,800-Year-Old Siberian Sacrificial Tomb Reveals Earliest Known Evidence of Cannabis Intoxication
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Thousands of years ago, in what is now Siberia, a mysterious ancient culture laid some of their dead to rest in an enormous burial mound.
paras.zh: 几千年前，在现在的西伯利亚，一种神秘的古代文化将一些死者埋葬在一个巨大的坟墓中。

paras.en: The kurgan, now known as Tunnug 1, was richly appointed – and its contents possibly gruesome.
paras.zh: 这个库尔干现在被称为 Tunnug 1，布置丰富，里面的内容可能令人毛骨悚然。

paras.en: The royal tomb contained elaborate grave goods, as well as the remains of dozens of sacrificed horses, many placed with human bones in arrangements that evoke ancient accounts of ghostly riders standing guard over Scythian kings.
paras.zh: 皇家陵墓中藏有精美的陪葬品，以及数十匹被牺牲的马匹的遗骸，其中许多马匹的遗骸上都安放着人骨，让人想起古代传说中幽灵骑士守护斯基泰国王的故事。

paras.en: Now, a new discovery suggests that a very familiar substance may have played a role in these funerary rites – cannabis.
paras.zh: 现在，一项新发现表明，一种非常熟悉的物质可能在这些丧葬仪式中发挥了作用——大麻。

paras.en: And not just the seeds buried with the dead. Analysis of human hair from the Arzhan Scythians interred in the kurgan has revealed compounds associated with the plant's intoxicating effects.
paras.zh: 不仅仅是与死者一起埋葬的种子。对埋藏在库尔干中的阿尔占斯基泰人的人类头发进行的分析揭示了与该植物的醉人作用相关的化合物。

paras.en: The findings, reported by an international study led by archaeologist Gino Caspari of the University of Bern in Switzerland, provide the earliest securely dated direct evidence yet of psychoactive cannabis use.
paras.zh: 瑞士伯尔尼大学考古学家吉诺·卡斯帕里领导的一项国际研究报告的这一发现提供了迄今为止最早的、有确切日期的精神活性大麻使用的直接证据。

paras.en: And it may have been used as part of the sacrificial rites.
paras.zh: 它可能被用作祭祀仪式的一部分。

paras.en: "In this princely tomb, the burials were accompanied by extensive horse sacrifices and, most likely, human sacrifices as well," Caspari says.
paras.zh: 卡斯帕里说：“在这座王陵中，埋葬时伴随着大量的马祭品，很可能还有活人祭品。”

paras.en: Tunnug 1 lies in the Uyuk Valley of southern Siberia, a region sometimes called the Valley of the Kings for the huge number of ancient Scythian burial mounds that can be found there.
paras.zh: Tunnug 1 位于西伯利亚南部的 Uyuk 山谷，该地区有时被称为帝王谷，因为那里可以找到大量古代斯基泰人的墓葬。

paras.en: Dating to around the early eighth century BCE, the monument is among the earliest known royal tombs associated with the Scythians, the horse-riding peoples whose cultures eventually spread across much of the Eurasian steppes – the Arzhan culture at the very onset of the Scythian period.
paras.zh: 这座纪念碑的历史可以追溯到公元前八世纪初左右，是已知最早与斯基泰人有关的皇家陵墓之一，斯基泰人是一个骑马的民族，他们的文化最终传播到了欧亚大草原的大部分地区，即斯基泰时期初期的阿尔赞文化。

paras.en: It was discovered in the 2010s, and archaeologists rapidly realized they had found something special – one of the oldest known Scythian royal tombs. And what a tomb it was.
paras.zh: 它于 2010 年代被发现，考古学家很快意识到他们发现了一些特别的东西——已知最古老的斯基泰皇家陵墓之一。那是一座什么样的坟墓啊。

paras.en: Measuring roughly 140 meters (460 feet) across, the enormous mound concealed an elaborate arrangement of wooden burial chambers, along with bronze ornaments, beads, weapons, and horse-riding equipment.
paras.zh: 这座巨大的土丘宽约 140 米（460 英尺），里面隐藏着精心布置的木制墓室，以及青铜装饰品、珠子、武器和骑马设备。

paras.en: Its scale and intricate construction suggest that the people who built it commanded considerable resources.
paras.zh: 它的规模和复杂的结构表明建造它的人拥有大量的资源。

paras.en: The new investigation focused on six individuals interred in four wooden burial structures within the mound – and something rather more humble than you might usually expect of a 'princely burial'.
paras.zh: 新的调查集中在土丘内四个木制墓葬结构中埋葬的六人，而且比你通常想象的“王子墓葬”要简陋得多。

paras.en: In and around the human burials, archaeologists discovered an extraordinary quantity of cannabis seeds – more than 1,000, many still intact after nearly three millennia.
paras.zh: 在人类墓葬中及其周围，考古学家发现了数量惊人的大麻种子——超过 1,000 颗，其中许多在近三千年后仍然完好无损。

paras.en: The seeds were small, resembling those of wild cannabis rather than modern domesticated varieties. And although cannabis is often associated with warmer climates, the plant grows naturally across temperate Central Asia, so it may have been gathered locally.
paras.zh: 这些种子很小，类似于野生大麻而不是现代驯化品种的种子。尽管大麻通常与温暖的气候联系在一起，但这种植物在中亚温带自然生长，因此它可能是在当地采集的。

paras.en: Their presence raised questions. Plant seeds don't tend to be included in elaborate burials unless they are culturally important in some way. So what was so important about these seeds?
paras.zh: 他们的出现引起了疑问。植物种子往往不会被包含在精心设计的墓葬中，除非它们在某种程度上具有重要的文化意义。那么这些种子有何重要意义呢？

paras.en: To find out, the researchers needed to dig a little deeper – chemically, anyway.
paras.zh: 为了找到答案，研究人员需要进行更深入的研究——无论如何，是从化学角度进行的。

paras.en: Cannabis plants vary in their production of intoxicating compounds, and the seeds alone couldn't reveal whether these ancient plants had been used for their psychoactive effects.
paras.zh: 大麻植物产生的令人陶醉的化合物各不相同，仅凭种子无法揭示这些古老植物是否已被用于其精神作用。

paras.en: But the researchers had another clue. Unlike many other soft tissues, hair is remarkably resistant to decomposition – and, as hair grows, traces of substances circulating through the body can become trapped within its keratin structure, creating a chemical record that remains long after death.
paras.zh: 但研究人员还有另一条线索。与许多其他软组织不同，头发具有显着的抗分解能力，而且随着头发的生长，在体内循环的微量物质可能会被困在其角蛋白结构中，从而形成一种化学记录，在死后很长一段时间内仍然存在。

paras.en: Human hair the tomb certainly had, too – preserved so perfectly it looks like it could have been taken from a living head yesterday, still bound up in braids.
paras.zh: 这座坟墓当然也有人类的头发--保存得如此完美，以至于看起来它昨天可能是从一个活生生的头上取下来的，仍然被辫子绑着。

paras.en: The researchers took samples of the hair and subjected them to mass spectrometry, looking for the telltale chemical signatures of cannabinoids preserved within.
paras.zh: 研究人员采集了头发的样本，并对其进行了质谱分析，以寻找保存在其中的大麻素的化学特征。

paras.en: In every one of the hair samples they tested, the results revealed clear chemical signals matching cannabinol (CBN), a compound that forms when tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) – the main intoxicating ingredient in cannabis – breaks down over time.
paras.zh: 在他们测试的每一个头发样本中，结果都显示出与大麻酚 (CBN) 相匹配的清晰化学信号，大麻酚 (CBN) 是大麻中主要致醉成分四氢大麻酚 (THC) 随着时间的推移分解时形成的化合物。

paras.en: The researchers also detected much weaker signals consistent with THC itself.
paras.zh: 研究人员还检测到与 THC 本身一致的微弱信号。

paras.en: Together, the findings provide compelling evidence that these ancient people had been exposed to psychoactive cannabis – likely on purpose.
paras.zh: 总之，这些发现提供了令人信服的证据，证明这些古代人曾接触过精神活性大麻——很可能是故意的。

paras.en: "The molecular traces in the hair and the cannabis seeds come from the same grave and suggest that cannabis was used for its intoxicating properties," Caspari says.
paras.zh: 卡斯帕里说：“头发和大麻种子中的分子痕迹来自同一个坟墓，表明大麻因其令人陶醉的特性而被使用。”

paras.en: That's a tantalizing result – because it raises more questions than it answers.
paras.zh: 这是一个诱人的结果——因为它提出的问题多于它给出的答案。

paras.en: While it seems pretty clear that the deceased had been exposed to cannabis, we don't know how – whether it was eaten, smoked, inhaled from passive exposure, or infused into a nice pot of tea.
paras.zh: 虽然很明显死者接触过大麻，但我们不知道是如何接触大麻的——是否是吃、吸、被动接触大麻，还是注入一壶好茶中。

paras.en: We also don't know what they had used it for… although the paper offers an intriguing possibility.
paras.zh: 我们也不知道他们用它做什么……尽管这篇论文提供了一个有趣的可能性。

paras.en: "The likely involvement of human sacrifice leading to the creation of a spectral cavalcade would have potentially made the plant a useful agent to calm individuals who were to be included in the rituals," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“人类献祭可能会导致幽灵队列的产生，这可能会使该植物成为安抚参加仪式的个体的有用剂。”

paras.en: The researchers are now sequencing the ancient cannabis remains, hoping to learn more about whether the plants were cultivated and how cannabis spread across the ancient world.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正在对古代大麻遗骸进行测序，希望更多地了解这些植物是否被种植以及大麻如何在古代世界传播。

paras.en: In the meantime, it serves to mark a new chapter in the long history of humanity's relationship with psychoactive substances.
paras.zh: 与此同时，它标志着人类与精神活性物质关系的悠久历史翻开了新的篇章。

paras.en: "Early cannabis use thus emerges not simply as a pharmacological curiosity but as an indication of how ancient societies experimented with and ritualized the psychoactive qualities of the botanical world," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“因此，早期大麻的使用不仅仅是一种药理学好奇心，而且表明古代社会如何实验和仪式化植物世界的精神活性品质。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学》杂志上。

articles.title: 400,000-year-old teeth reveal a stunning twist in human evolution

paras.en: 400,000-year-old teeth reveal a stunning twist in human evolution
paras.zh: 40万年前的牙齿揭示了人类进化的惊人转折

paras.en: - A groundbreaking discovery is rewriting the story of human evolution, revealing that an ancient human species once thought to be an evolutionary dead end may have left genetic traces in people alive today. By extracting proteins from 400,000-year-old Homo erectus teeth discovered in China, scientists uncovered evidence suggesting that these early humans interbred with Denisovans, another mysterious ancient human group. That genetic connection may have eventually reached modern populations in the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and other parts of Southeast Asia.
paras.zh: - 一项突破性的发现正在改写人类进化的故事，揭示了曾经被认为是进化死胡同的古代人类物种可能在今天活着的人类身上留下了遗传痕迹。通过从中国发现的 40 万年前直立人牙齿中提取蛋白质，科学家发现了证据表明这些早期人类与另一个神秘的古代人类群体丹尼索瓦人杂交。这种基因联系可能最终传到了菲律宾、巴布亚新几内亚和东南亚其他地区的现代人群。

paras.en: For most of the 20th century, the model of human origins was a tree: with the trunk dividing into branches, and then twigs. Each species of human relative (hominin) was a neat, single branch.
paras.zh: 在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，人类起源的模型是一棵树：树干分为树枝，然后是细枝。人类亲戚（古人类）的每个物种都是一个整齐的单一分支。

paras.en: As an undergraduate, I was taught that Homo sapiens was one of these branches that emerged in Africa, spread across the world, and displaced every archaic human it encountered.
paras.zh: 作为一名本科生，我被告知智人是在非洲出现、传播到世界各地并取代了它遇到的每一个古人类的分支之一。

paras.en: Neanderthals, Homo erectus, and other ancient relatives were evolutionary dead ends – unfortunate cousins who left no descendants. In the 30 years since I left university, those early lessons are now radically revised.
paras.zh: 尼安德特人、直立人以及其他远古亲戚在进化上都陷入了死胡同——不幸的近亲没有留下后代。自从我离开大学以来的 30 年里，那些早期的课程现在已经得到了彻底的修改。

paras.en: That neat replacement story is now comprehensively wrong, largely thanks to studies like the one published in Nature by Qiaomei Fu from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and colleagues. The paper achieves something that would have seemed impossible a decade ago: it recovers meaningful biological information from H. erectus fossils far too old for DNA.
paras.zh: 这个简洁的替代故事现在是完全错误的，这很大程度上要归功于中国科学院傅巧梅及其同事在《自然》杂志上发表的研究。这篇论文实现了十年前看似不可能的事情：它从对于 DNA 来说太古老的直立人化石中恢复了有意义的生物信息。

paras.en: Instead of genetic sequences, the team extracted ancient proteins from the enamel of six teeth from three Chinese sites – Zhoukoudian (which, in the early 20th century, produced fossil remains known as “Peking Man”), Hexian and Sunjiadong – all dating to around 400,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 研究小组没有从基因序列中提取古代蛋白质，而是从中国三个遗址——周口店（20世纪初，产生了被称为“北京人”的化石遗骸）、和县和孙家洞——的六颗牙齿的牙釉质中提取了古代蛋白质，这些遗址的历史都可以追溯到大约40万年前。

paras.en: Homo erectus is widely regarded as the first hominin to leave Africa; the evidence suggests this species had moved into Eurasia nearly two million years ago. It remains the most geographically widespread human ancestor that ever lived. The new study indicates that Homo erectus exchanged genes (probably through interbreeding) with Denisovans in East Asia roughly 400,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 直立人被广泛认为是第一个离开非洲的古人类。有证据表明，该物种在近两百万年前就已迁入欧亚大陆。它仍然是有史以来地理分布最广泛的人类祖先。这项新研究表明，大约 40 万年前，直立人与东亚的丹尼索瓦人交换了基因（可能是通过杂交）。

paras.en: The study suggests that some of that genetic legacy, it now appears, was passed on to living people in the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and across south-east Asia.
paras.zh: 该研究表明，现在看来，其中一些遗传遗产被遗传给了菲律宾、巴布亚新几内亚和整个东南亚的现存人们。

paras.en: Tooth enamel is the hardest tissue in the body, and its proteins survive long after DNA has degraded beyond recovery. What the team found in those proteins is striking. All six specimens share a previously unknown amino acid variant – a tiny molecular signature, a single letter changed in the protein sequence, never seen in any other hominin alive or dead.
paras.zh: 牙釉质是体内最坚硬的组织，其蛋白质在 DNA 降解至无法恢复的情况下仍能存活很长时间。研究小组在这些蛋白质中的发现是惊人的。所有六个样本都有一个以前未知的氨基酸变异——一个微小的分子特征，蛋白质序列中的一个字母发生了变化，这在任何其他活着或死亡的古人类中从未见过。

paras.en: This variant clusters these east Asian H. erectus into a distinct group, confirming their identity and settling a long-running debate about whether the unusual Hexian fossils were H. erectus at all. A second variant they share, however, is not unique to H. erectus.
paras.zh: 这一变体将这些东亚直立人聚集成一个独特的群体，确认了它们的身份，并解决了关于不寻常的和县化石是否是直立人的长期争论。然而，它们共有的第二种变异并不是直立人所独有的。

paras.en: It also appears in Denisovans – a mysterious archaic (non-Homo sapiens) human group known mainly from a cave in Siberia. The corresponding genetic variant turns up in living people at frequencies of 21% in the Philippines and about 1% in India, distributed in a pattern that matches what we’d expect if it entered modern humans via Denisovan ancestry.
paras.zh: 它也出现在丹尼索瓦人中——一个神秘的古老（非智人）人类群体，主要来自西伯利亚的一个洞穴。相应的基因变异在菲律宾的活人中出现的频率为 21%，在印度的频率约为 1%，其分布模式与我们预期的分布模式相符，如果它通过丹尼索瓦人血统进入现代人类的话。

paras.en: The most reasonable interpretation is that H. erectus populations in east Asia passed this variant to Denisovans through interbreeding, and Denisovans later passed it on to the ancestors of modern south-east Asians and Oceanians. This transfer of genetic material from one species to another is known as introgression.
paras.zh: 最合理的解释是，东亚的直立人种群通过杂交将这种变异遗传给了丹尼索瓦人，而丹尼索瓦人后来又将其遗传给了现代东南亚人和大洋洲人的祖先。这种遗传物质从一个物种到另一个物种的转移称为基因渗入。

paras.en: The lineage we once thought was a dead end has, it turns out, left a small but detectable trace in living human genomes – a molecular thread connecting a Peking Man tooth to living people in Asia.
paras.zh: 事实证明，我们曾经认为是死胡同的谱系在活人类基因组中留下了微小但可检测的痕迹——一条将北京猿人牙齿与活生生的亚洲人连接起来的分子线。

paras.en: But the significance of today’s paper extends well beyond the specific variant or the specific populations involved. What it really shows is that interbreeding between archaic human lineages was not exceptional. It was routine.
paras.zh: 但今天这篇论文的意义远远超出了所涉及的特定变体或特定人群。它真正表明的是，古代人类血统之间的杂交并不罕见。这是例行公事。

paras.en: Every major hominin lineage we have been able to examine genomically shows admixture. Modern humans outside Africa carry roughly 2% Neanderthal DNA. Papuans and Aboriginal Australians carry an additional 2–5% Denisovan ancestry.
paras.zh: 我们能够在基因组上检查的每个主要古人类谱系都显示出混合物。非洲以外的现代人类携带大约 2% 的尼安德特人 DNA。巴布亚人和澳大利亚原住民还有 2-5% 的丹尼索瓦血统。

paras.en: West African populations carry genetic signatures from an unidentified archaic lineage. Even Denisovans themselves, as today’s study adds further weight to, received gene flow from something older and more diverged — likely H. erectus.
paras.zh: 西非人口携带着来自不明古老血统的遗传特征。正如今天的研究进一步强调的那样，甚至丹尼索瓦人本身也从更古老、更分化的生物（可能是直立人）那里接收了基因流。

paras.en: A 2019 review in the American Journal of Physical Anthropology documents at least three distinct introgression events from Denisovan-like populations into south-east Asian and Oceanic ancestors alone, some occurring as recently as 20,000 years ago. The picture is not one of clean lineages but of a tangled web of contact and exchange extending across millions of years.
paras.zh: 《美国体质人类学杂志》2019 年的一篇评论记录了至少三起不同的类丹尼索瓦人向东南亚和大洋洲祖先的渐渗事件，其中一些发生在 2 万年前。这幅图画并不是一个干净的血统，而是一个绵延数百万年的错综复杂的接触和交流网络。

paras.en: The implications are far-reaching. Our genomes are not the product of a single unbroken lineage emerging from Africa. They are mosaics, assembled from contributions by multiple archaic groups, each adapted to its own regional environment.
paras.zh: 其影响是深远的。我们的基因组并不是来自非洲的单一完整谱系的产物。它们是由多个古老团体的贡献拼凑而成的马赛克，每个团体都适应自己的区域环境。

paras.en: Some of the Denisovan-derived variants in Papuan genomes, for instance, appear to influence immune function. The H. erectus-derived variant identified today has unknown functional consequences – that remains an open question – but the precedent from other gene variants that have introgressed (genes that have passed from one species into another) suggests that adaptation to new environments may have been part of the story.
paras.zh: 例如，巴布亚基因组中的一些源自丹尼索瓦人的变体似乎会影响免疫功能。今天发现的直立人衍生的变异具有未知的功能后果——这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题——但其他基因变异（基因从一个物种传递到另一个物种）的先例表明，对新环境的适应可能是故事的一部分。

paras.en: Perhaps most intriguing is what the new paper implies about all the populations we cannot yet study. H. erectus survived in Indonesia until perhaps 100,000 years ago. Homo floresiensis, the diminutive “hobbit” species, was present on Flores when modern humans arrived. Another human lineage, Homo luzonensis, occupied the Philippines.
paras.zh: 也许最有趣的是这篇新论文对我们尚无法研究的所有人群的暗示。直立人直到大约十万年前才在印度尼西亚生存。当现代人类到达弗洛勒斯岛时，弗洛勒斯人（Homo floresiensis）是一种小型的“霍比特人”物种。另一个人类谱系，吕宋人，占领了菲律宾。

paras.en: None of these populations have yielded DNA, and until today none had yielded any molecular data at all. Were they also absorbed, at least partially, into the human populations that replaced them? The genomic evidence from living people has not, so far, detected their signal clearly – but the tools available until recently were blunt instruments.
paras.zh: 这些种群都没有产生 DNA，而且直到今天还没有产生任何分子数据。他们是否也被（至少部分地）吸收到取代他们的人类群体中？迄今为止，来自活人的基因组证据尚未清楚地检测到它们的信号，但直到最近可用的工具都是钝器。

paras.en: The proteomic approach demonstrated in today’s paper offers a way forward. If proteins can be recovered from H. erectus enamel at 400,000 years, the same approach applied to floresiensis or luzonensis material might finally reveal whether those lineages, too, contributed something to the humans who came after them.
paras.zh: 今天的论文中展示的蛋白质组学方法提供了一条前进的道路。如果能够在 40 万年前从直立人牙釉质中回收蛋白质，那么对弗洛勒斯人和吕宋人材料应用相同的方法可能最终会揭示这些谱系是否也对他们之后的人类做出了贡献。

paras.en: The old metaphor of a tree – a single trunk branching into distinct species – has been quietly replaced in the scientific literature. It might be better to consider the process as a braided river, with many channels running partly together and partly apart, exchanging water continuously.
paras.zh: 树的古老比喻——一根树干分出不同的物种——在科学文献中已悄然被取代。最好将这个过程视为一条辫状河，许多河道部分在一起，部分分开，不断交换水。

paras.en: This new study is one more confirmation that when ancient human populations disappeared, they left traces of themselves behind.
paras.zh: 这项新研究再次证实，当古代人类消失时，他们留下了自己的痕迹。

paras.en: Materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Sally Christine Reynolds, Associate Professor in Hominin Palaeoecology, Bournemouth University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由对话提供。原文由伯恩茅斯大学古人类古生态学副教授 Sally Christine Reynolds 撰写。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: A clever molecular trick unlocks previously impossible properties in glass

paras.en: A clever molecular trick unlocks previously impossible properties in glass
paras.zh: 巧妙的分子技巧解锁了玻璃中以前不可能的特性

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered how to reprogram the internal structure of glass using a special molecule that rearranges chemical bonds while lowering the melting temperature. The breakthrough could unlock entirely new glass materials with precisely controlled magnetic and optical properties, opening possibilities for advanced electronics, sensors, and other technologies.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了如何使用一种特殊的分子重新编程玻璃的内部结构，该分子可以重新排列化学键，同时降低熔化温度。这一突破可以解锁具有精确控制的磁和光学特性的全新玻璃材料，为先进电子、传感器和其他技术带来可能性。

paras.en: Scientists have developed a new way to change the internal structure of glass while it is being made, giving them greater control over properties such as magnetism and the way the material interacts with light. The discovery could open the door to advanced glasses with capabilities that were previously difficult or impossible to achieve.
paras.zh: 科学家们开发出了一种在玻璃制造过程中改变其内部结构的新方法，使他们能够更好地控制磁性以及材料与光相互作用的方式等特性。这一发现可能为先进眼镜打开大门，这些眼镜具有以前难以或不可能实现的功能。

paras.en: The breakthrough comes from a collaboration involving TU Dortmund University, Paderborn University, the University of Duisburg-Essen, and the University of Oxford. Published in Nature Materials, the research demonstrates how adding a particular organic molecule during the melting process can rearrange chemical bonds within certain types of glass.
paras.zh: 这一突破来自多特蒙德工业大学、帕德博恩大学、杜伊斯堡-埃森大学和牛津大学的合作。该研究发表在《自然材料》上，展示了在熔化过程中添加特定有机分子如何重新排列某些类型玻璃内的化学键。

paras.en: The method also allows these materials to melt at much lower temperatures, preventing the damage that would otherwise occur during manufacturing. Such specialized glasses have potential applications in gas storage, batteries, optical technologies, and catalysis.
paras.zh: 该方法还允许这些材料在低得多的温度下熔化，从而防止在制造过程中发生损坏。这种特种玻璃在气体储存、电池、光学技术和催化领域具有潜在的应用前景。

paras.en: A Molecular Trick That Changes Glass From Within
paras.zh: 从内部改变玻璃的分子技巧

paras.en: "We have found a way to chemically modify the structure of glasses derived from so-called metal-organic framework compounds - or MOFs for short - right during the manufacturing process," explains Prof. Dr. Sebastian Henke from TU Dortmund University, who led the study.
paras.zh: 领导这项研究的多特蒙德工业大学 Sebastian Henke 教授解释说：“我们找到了一种方法，可以在制造过程中对由所谓的金属有机骨架化合物（简称 MOF）衍生的玻璃结构进行化学修饰。”

paras.en: The key ingredient is a molecule called 1,10-phenanthroline. When introduced during production, it performs two important tasks. It reduces the temperature needed to melt the material while also changing how metal atoms connect with surrounding molecules.
paras.zh: 关键成分是一种称为 1,10-菲咯啉的分子。当在生产过程中引入时，它会执行两项重要任务。它降低了熔化材料所需的温度，同时也改变了金属原子与周围分子的连接方式。

paras.en: This combination allows researchers to create glass with magnetic or light-emitting characteristics that previously could not be achieved without exposing the material to potentially destructive temperatures.
paras.zh: 这种组合使研究人员能够制造出具有磁性或发光特性的玻璃，而以前如果不将材料暴露在具有潜在破坏性的温度下，就无法实现这种特性。

paras.en: To understand why this approach matters, it helps to consider how glass normally forms. When a liquid cools quickly enough, its atoms become locked into a disordered arrangement rather than forming the repeating pattern found in crystals.
paras.zh: 要理解这种方法的重要性，需要考虑玻璃通常是如何形成的。当液体冷却得足够快时，其原子就会被锁定为无序排列，而不是形成晶体中的重复图案。

paras.en: "Normally, glass is formed when a molten liquid cools rapidly. The solid structure then sets without the atoms arranging themselves in a regular pattern. Until now, researchers often had to accept the chemistry of these glasses as dictated by the starting material," explains Prof. Henke.
paras.zh: “通常情况下，玻璃是在熔融液体快速冷却时形成的。固体结构随后会凝固，原子不会以规则的方式排列。到目前为止，研究人员常常不得不接受这些玻璃的化学成分是由起始材料决定的，”亨克教授解释道。

paras.en: The new findings show that scientists can exert much greater control over this process.
paras.zh: 新发现表明科学家可以对这一过程施加更大的控制。

paras.en: Metal-organic frameworks are materials built from metal centers connected by organic compounds. By introducing phenanthroline while these materials are molten, researchers can change the chemical connections within the structure before the glass solidifies.
paras.zh: 金属有机框架是由有机化合物连接的金属中心构建的材料。通过在这些材料熔化时引入菲咯啉，研究人员可以在玻璃凝固之前改变结构内的化学连接。

paras.en: "The crucial point is that the molecule does not simply remain as a filler," Prof. Henke continues. "It enters into a reaction. So we are altering the chemistry at precisely the moment when the material is still liquid."
paras.zh: “关键的一点是，该分子不仅仅只是作为填充剂，”亨克教授继续说道。 “它会发生反应。因此，我们正是在材料仍呈液态时改变化学性质。”

paras.en: How a Single Molecule Restructures Glass
paras.zh: 单分子如何重组玻璃

paras.en: The researchers added phenanthroline to their starting materials before heating them. Once the mixture begins to melt, the molecule does more than simply lower the temperature required for melting. It actively participates in chemical reactions that reorganize the glass network.
paras.zh: 研究人员在加热之前将菲咯啉添加到起始材料中。一旦混合物开始熔化，分子的作用不仅仅是降低熔化所需的温度。它积极参与重组玻璃网络的化学反应。

paras.en: The process changes the immediate surroundings of metal atoms by modifying their connections to neighboring molecules.
paras.zh: 该过程通过改变金属原子与邻近分子的连接来改变金属原子的直接周围环境。

paras.en: "As a flux, the substance lowers the temperature at which the material melts; as a chemical agent, the molecule binds directly to the metal atoms and partially displaces old bonds. In the molten state, the molecule interferes with what is known as the coordination environment. This term describes how many neighbors surround a single atom. Because the new molecule binds more strongly to the metal centers, the number of neighbors increases," explains Prof. Henke.
paras.zh: “作为助熔剂，该物质降低了材料熔化的温度；作为化学试剂，分子直接与金属原子结合并部分取代旧的键。在熔融状态下，分子会干扰所谓的配位环境。这个术语描述了单个原子周围有多少个邻居。因为新分子与金属中心的结合更牢固，所以邻居的数量增加，”Henke教授解释道。

paras.en: These interactions trigger a substantial rearrangement of the internal glass structure. Importantly, the researchers can control how extensively the material changes simply by adjusting the amount of phenanthroline added.
paras.zh: 这些相互作用引发了内部玻璃结构的实质性重新排列。重要的是，研究人员只需调整菲咯啉的添加量即可控制材料变化的程度。

paras.en: This gives scientists a practical way to tune the properties of glass during manufacturing rather than relying entirely on the chemistry of the original ingredients.
paras.zh: 这为科学家们提供了一种在制造过程中调整玻璃性能的实用方法，而不是完全依赖原始成分的化学成分。

paras.en: Lower Temperatures Prevent Damage to Glass
paras.zh: 较低的温度可防止玻璃损坏

paras.en: Another major advantage of the discovery is that it overcomes a longstanding problem in manufacturing specialized glasses.
paras.zh: 这一发现的另一个主要优点是它克服了制造特种玻璃的长期存在的问题。

paras.en: Some of the materials investigated are unable to withstand the temperatures normally required to melt them. Instead of becoming usable glass, they begin to break down, damaging their structure and producing unwanted impurities.
paras.zh: 所研究的一些材料无法承受通常熔化它们所需的温度。它们没有成为可用的玻璃，而是开始分解，破坏其结构并产生不需要的杂质。

paras.en: The new molecular approach avoids much of this problem by allowing the materials to melt under gentler conditions.
paras.zh: 新的分子方法通过允许材料在更温和的条件下熔化，在很大程度上避免了这个问题。

paras.en: "Thanks to this molecular trick, the material melts at significantly lower temperatures and remains stable. Studies on cobalt-containing glasses have shown that this gentler process prevents the formation of harmful decomposition products," explains Prof. Dr. Matthias Bauer from Paderborn University.
paras.zh: “由于这种分子技巧，该材料在显着较低的温度下熔化并保持稳定。对含钴玻璃的研究表明，这种温和的过程可以防止有害分解产物的形成，”帕德博恩大学的 Matthias Bauer 教授解释说。

paras.en: Preventing these unwanted byproducts is particularly important when studying magnetic properties. Impurities can interfere with measurements and conceal the material's actual magnetic behavior. By keeping the glass chemically stable, the researchers can observe these effects more clearly.
paras.zh: 在研究磁特性时，防止这些不需要的副产品尤为重要。杂质会干扰测量并隐藏材料的实际磁性行为。通过保持玻璃的化学稳定性，研究人员可以更清楚地观察这些效应。

paras.en: Advanced X-ray Measurements Confirm the Changes
paras.zh: 先进的 X 射线测量证实了这些变化

paras.en: To verify that the molecular treatment genuinely altered the glass, the research team turned to sophisticated analytical techniques.
paras.zh: 为了验证分子处理确实改变了玻璃，研究小组转向了复杂的分析技术。

paras.en: Studying glass presents a challenge because its atoms do not follow the regular, repeating arrangement found in crystalline materials. This limits what conventional X-ray methods can reveal about its internal structure.
paras.zh: 研究玻璃是一个挑战，因为它的原子不遵循晶体材料中规则的重复排列。这限制了传统 X 射线方法揭示其内部结构的能力。

paras.en: Prof. Bauer explains: "Instead, we used X-ray absorption spectroscopy, amongst other techniques. This method enabled us to investigate the immediate surroundings of the cobalt atoms."
paras.zh: Bauer 教授解释说：“相反，我们使用了 X 射线吸收光谱法等技术。这种方法使我们能够研究钴原子的直接周围环境。”

paras.en: The measurements provided strong evidence that the new molecule changes the arrangement of atoms around the metal centers.
paras.zh: 测量结果提供了强有力的证据，证明新分子改变了金属中心周围原子的排列。

paras.en: Although the cobalt atoms maintained the same chemical state (oxidation state), their local surroundings changed considerably. The bonds connecting them to nearby molecules were reorganized to accommodate the added phenanthroline.
paras.zh: 尽管钴原子保持相同的化学状态（氧化态），但它们的局部环境发生了很大变化。连接它们与附近分子的键被重组以适应添加的菲咯啉。

paras.en: These observations confirmed that the method does more than simply help the material melt. It changes the underlying chemistry of the glass itself.
paras.zh: 这些观察结果证实，该方法不仅仅是帮助材料熔化。它改变了玻璃本身的基本化学成分。

paras.en: A New Generation of Glass With Tunable Properties
paras.zh: 具有可调特性的新一代玻璃

paras.en: The researchers also demonstrated that their approach works beyond the original materials they investigated. Successful experiments with carboxylate-based framework structures suggest that the technique could be applied to a broader range of glass materials.
paras.zh: 研究人员还证明，他们的方法的效果超出了他们研究的原始材料。基于羧酸盐的框架结构的成功实验表明该技术可以应用于更广泛的玻璃材料。

paras.en: This versatility is especially promising because it transforms the melting stage of production into an opportunity to design new material properties.
paras.zh: 这种多功能性特别有前途，因为它将生产的熔化阶段转变为设计新材料特性的机会。

paras.en: Prof. Henke summarizes the significance for the future: "The melt is no longer a rigid intermediate state. It becomes a reaction space in which we can program the structure."
paras.zh: Henke 教授总结了其对未来的意义：“熔体不再是刚性的中间状态。它变成了一个反应空间，我们可以在其中对结构进行编程。”

paras.en: The ability to precisely modify metal centers could eventually lead to advanced glass components designed for specific technological purposes.
paras.zh: 精确修改金属中心的能力最终可能会导致为特定技术目的而设计的先进玻璃组件。

paras.en: Potential applications include chemical catalysts, sensors, and optoelectronic devices that use interactions between light and electricity. Researchers could also develop materials capable of controlling magnetic behavior, manipulating light, or influencing chemical reactions with greater precision.
paras.zh: 潜在的应用包括化学催化剂、传感器和利用光与电之间相互作用的光电设备。研究人员还可以开发能够更精确地控制磁性行为、操纵光或影响化学反应的材料。

paras.en: By turning molten glass into a material whose chemistry can be deliberately adjusted, the discovery offers a new route toward specialized glasses with properties that conventional manufacturing techniques could not easily produce.
paras.zh: 通过将熔融玻璃转变为化学性质可以有意调整的材料，这一发现为制造具有传统制造技术无法轻易生产的特性的特种玻璃提供了一条新途径。
